name: Peter Welch
subject: What unites us
disclaimer_text: PAID FOR BY WELCH FOR VERMONT
body:
Democrats won historic electoral victories across the country at all levels of government.

# [](https://act.welchforvermont.com/go/144?t=2&akid=1409%2E61531%2Ep0ZOJ7)
Hi there,
As you know, Democrats won historic electoral victories across the country at all levels of government. In the Senate, we defied the odds and took the majority.
We flipped seats in every region: Maine, Texas, Iowa, Mississippi, Kansas, and Alaska.
Those victorious candidates come from disparate backgrounds: preachers, physicians, paralympians, loggers.
They don’t agree on everything, but their campaigns all focused on one thing: lowering costs for working Americans.
Corporations are posting record profits. Billionaires are getting tax cuts. And the prices on the things Americans buy every day are rising faster than anyone can keep up with.
It’s wrong.
That fight is what will unite all of us come January when we take over the majority.
That fight must be the top priority on our legislative agenda.
I can’t wait to get started,
Peter

Peter, you can practically smell the desperation. Republican gerrymanders backfired horribly this year, angering voters across the country and costing the GOP seats in the very states they tried to rig. But Republican operatives are frantically defending their map manipulations — take a look: “‘Redistricting saved Republicans seats in Texas that otherwise would have been lost in this wave,’ [president] of the National Republican Redistricting Trust said in an interview...” — The Washington Post “Florida Gov. Ron DeSantis (R) argued that his redistricting earlier this year saved two Republican seats that would not have survived under the old map, even as the GOP lost in all four districts the map was designed to flip.” — The Washington Post It might sound delusional, but there’s a clear reason they want to believe that their mid-decade redraws were effective: it’s their key strategy for 2028. [Everyone needs to read between the lines here: More GOP redraws are on the way. Now he’s throwing a full-blown temper tantrum on Truth Social, accusing me and my Democratic colleagues of "extortion" and ordering his Attorney General to investigate us. Trump is panicking — and he should be. He spent years turning the White House into a personal piggy bank, taking pay-to-play ballroom donations, watching Jared Kushner rake in hundreds of millions from foreign powers, and ignoring human rights abuses at our border. He thought he would never have to answer to anyone. Then the American voters delivered an absolute rout, swept Democrats into the majority, and handed us the gavel. Now that constitutional oversight is coming for him, he claims holding corrupt politicians accountable is "illegal". Hear me loud and clear: Demanding accountability is not extortion. It is our constitutional duty. Trump can try to weaponize the Department of Justice. He can order his Attorney General to issue threats. But I will never be intimidated by a rattled bully. The days of uncontained corruption end the moment I take the chair. name: President Donald J. Trump
subject: I'm going to be honest about Election Day.
disclaimer_text: Paid for by Never Surrender, Inc
body:
Are you there?
| | | | [](https://link.win.donaldjtrump.)
---
I penned this message for you myself.

This is important, and I want you to hear it from me directly.
[MESSAGE FROM TRUMP](https://link.win.donaldjtrump.)
This fall season has been a real wake-up call for our movement.

Outside my Oval Office window, the leaves are turning beautiful reds, golds, and oranges, but another, very different change is also happening in Washington, D.C.

I’ll be honest with you: what happened on Election Night wasn’t what we wanted to see.

It hurt. I know it hurt you too because you’ve put your heart into this. You always have.
Now, across our country, dangerous, Radical Democrats are set to take office in just a few short weeks.
[STAND WITH TRUMP](https://link.win.donaldjtrump.)
Their agenda is simple and ugly:

**DESTROY the American Golden Age that we have built together.**

They want to throw open our borders.

Pack the Supreme Court.

Eliminate Voter ID.

_They want to erase everything we fought so hard to protect._

**But here is the truth that fills me with fire and gratitude this Thanksgiving season: they have not broken us. Not even close.
**
And although we have stumbled, we have not been broken - and we will never be broken.
[STAND WITH TRUMP](https://link.win.donaldjtrump.)
Because our movement is filled with patriots like yourself: those brave Americans who have always stood for our nation even when the going has been tough, when the headlines have turned against us, and when others have walked away.

That kind of loyalty is rare, and it means everything to me.

**You are the backbone of the greatest political movement in American history.**
And although the leaves outside may be falling, MAGA will remain standing.
[STAND WITH TRUMP](https://link.win.donaldjtrump.)
So as we begin to travel and gather with our loved ones this Thanksgiving season, I want you to feel two things at once:
1\. This fight is far from over. The Radical Left is more energized - and more dangerous - than ever.

2\. My solemn vow to you: that I will NEVER surrender our fight to Make America Great Again, no matter what they throw at me.

**_I will still fight for secure borders._** **_I will still fight for free and fair elections._** **_I will still fight for a country that puts America First._** **_I will still fight for the future our children deserve._**

Together, we will continue to **FIGHT! FIGHT! FIGHT!**
[STAND WITH TRUMP](https://link.win.donaldjtrump.)
This is our time to dig deeper, stand taller, and come back stronger than ever.
**[Please, if you are financially able, can I count on your support for just $20.27? Your contribution today could be the deciding factor in determining MAGA’s future in 2027.](https://link.win.donaldjtrump.)
**
Thank you & God bless you.

[](https://link.win.donaldjtrump.)
[STAND WITH TRUMP](https://link.win.donaldjtrump.)

name: Mark Kelly
subject: It’s time to stop Donald Trump’s arch
disclaimer_text: Paid For By Mark Kelly for Senate
body:
I am in complete opposition to this arch, and we have to stop it.
#

Team,
Hundreds of thousands of veterans are buried at Arlington National Cemetery, going all the way back to the Civil War. Many of them made the ultimate sacrifice, giving their lives in service to our nation. That’s a sacrifice few can truly understand, and one that deserves the respect of every single American.
That’s why Arlington is so special. If you’ve ever been, you know: It’s quiet, but powerful. It’s a symbol of the debt we owe to the men and women buried there, at eternal rest. Each of them earned their place.
Donald Trump doesn’t get that, and he never will. And that’s why he wants to drop a 250-foot tall arch dedicated entirely to himself at Arlington. An arch that would quite literally put the graves of fallen soldiers in Trump’s shadow and President John F. Kennedy’s final resting place and the eternal flame.
I am in complete opposition to this arch, and we have to stop it. Today, I’m asking you to join me.
[**Add your name alongside the thousands of others who stand against Donald Trump’s triumphal arch. We need as many people as we can to sign on today. It’s a small act, but it’s how we’ll send a clear message to Trump and the Republican Party: The American people won’t let this happen.**](https://act.markkelly.com/signup/Stop_the_arch/?source=em261119-1-MS&akid=6827%2E6688874%2ESmrOhl)
**[STOP THE ARCH](https://act.markkelly.com/signup/Stop_the_arch/?source=em261119-1-MS&akid=6827%2E6688874%2ESmrOhl)**
Thank you in advance for signing on.
Mark

Paid For By Mark Kelly for Senate
This email was sent to dpwillis67@gmail.com. Email is a very important way we communicate with supporters like you, but if you're receiving too many you can sign up for [fewer emails here](https://act.markkelly.com/signup/receive-fewer-emails/?t=1&akid=6827%2E6688874%2ESmrOhl). And while we'd hate to see you go, you can [ unsubscribe here](https://act.markkelly.com/unsubscribe/unsubscribe?t=2&akid=6827%2E6688874%2ESmrOhl).
Mark Kelly was a Captain in the U.S. Navy and astronaut. Peter Willis,

🚨The fight to stop Congress from racing forward with a plan to all but
fuse the U.S. and Israeli militaries is on — and we have just days to stop
it before it’s too late! 🚨

Leaders in Congress will meet in the coming days to try to hammer out an
agreement for the National Defense Authorization Act (NDAA). They’re
hoping the public doesn't notice that Trump and Netanyahu snuck a
terrifying provision into the bill, merging parts of U.S. and Israeli
defense industries.

We noticed. And we’re raising hell to stop it.

[ https://act.ourrevolution.com/go/40136?source=email-20261119&t=1011&akid=11614%2E5885482%2EkgJQyw ]Headline: Congress quietly moves to integrate US and Israeli militaries

to stop this before it’s too late, and we’re locked into an even CLOSER
relationship with Israel, with even less oversight.

[ https://act.ourrevolution.com/go/40136?source=email-20261119&t=1012&akid=11614%2E5885482%2EkgJQyw ]We have just days. Will you urgently add your name to show Congress the
public will not stand for MORE integration with the Israeli military?

[ https://act.ourrevolution.com/go/40136?source=email-20261119&t=1013&akid=11614%2E5885482%2EkgJQyw ]ADD YOUR NAME

is not there. On election day, he acknowledged that the US-Israel
relationship had become a political liability. So he and Netanyahu have a
plan to lock in the relationship outside of public view: Section 219,
which would supersize weapons deals, surveillance tech, and intelligence
sharing for YEARS to come, stripping away even the limited Congressional
checks that exist today.

It’s not just Trump. Earlier this week, Hakeem Jeffries refused to say his
view on Section 219.

Our new Post Election Survey of over 4,000 Our Revolution supporters found
that stopping the Iran war and stopping more bombs going to Israel should
be the NUMBER ONE priority of the new Congress. So we’re going all in to
make sure Congress gets that message.

[ https://act.ourrevolution.com/go/40136?source=email-20261119&t=1015&akid=11614%2E5885482%2EkgJQyw ]Let’s make sure Congress gets an avalanche of public opposition to
Section 219 RIGHT NOW, as leaders are meeting to decide a way forward. Add
your name now: Tell the Senate to strip Section 219 from the NDAA before
it’s too late!

[ https://act.ourrevolution.com/go/40136?source=email-20261119&t=1016&akid=11614%2E5885482%2EkgJQyw ]ADD YOUR NAME

When we organize, we win.

That’s what Getting Stuff Done means to me,

your Governor.

Calling out the problems isn’t enough. Calling out Trump’s chaos and
cruelty isn’t enough. We need to take real steps to fix it — and that’s
exactly what we’ve done for nearly four years here in Pennsylvania.

subject: every man needs to learn this survival skill ASAP
body:

For almost all of human history, there was one thing every man was expected to know how to do: Go into the woods and come back with meat for his family. Not buy it. Not order it. Get it, with his own hands, from the land around him. Your grandfather could do it. His father certainly could. Somewhere in the last two generations, most American men quietly lost the skill and never noticed, because the grocery store was always open. Here is the uncomfortable question: **If the trucks stopped running tomorrow, could you feed your family?** The shelves go bare in about three days. Your stockpile lasts a few weeks, maybe a few months. After that, the only food that doesn’t run out is the food that’s still walking around. And in America, that food is deer. More than 30 million whitetails. Every state but one. One doe is 40 to 50 pounds of lean red meat. No other food source in this country is that abundant, that widespread, or that close to your back door. That is why knowing how to hunt, kill, skin and cook a deer is not a hobby. It is a survival skill, and it is one every man owes his family. [Get the Complete Deer Hunter’s Bundle: 3 Books + 2 Skinning Knives + Leather Sheath](https://links.tacticalusa.com/a/1534/click/7568/11767687/6bc36d74e377fce4b96152017f97592d3971ad7a/e2cb5c80fa232a5db0d83b0ecb67642c9fc1f721) The problem is that “knowing how to hunt a deer” is actually four separate skills, and a man who is missing any one of them ends up with nothing: You have to find and kill the animal. You have to get it cooled, gutted and butchered before the meat spoils. You have to preserve it without a processor, and maybe without a freezer. You have to cook it so your family will actually eat it. Most hunters are weak in two of those. Most non-hunters have none of them. The Complete Hunter’s Bundle covers all four, with the knives to do the work: **Book One: The American Deer Hunting Handbook (231 pages)** How to beat a deer’s nose, eyes and ears. How to hunt the wind, read rubs and scrapes, and pick the spot that produces. Written for the experienced hunter, the beginner, and the man who may someday need to find and kill a deer with no stand, no familiar property, and no one to tell him where to sit. 22 diagrams. **Book Two: The American Deer Skinning Handbook (249 pages)** What to do the first night, step by step. Field dressing, the gutless method, a cooling decision tree for 30°, 50° and 70° nights. The whole-carcass cut map through shoulders, backstraps, tenderloins and hindquarters. Jerky, canning, and a survival appendix for when there is no ice, no freezer and no electricity. 26 diagrams and cut maps. Built so a man who has never processed a deer can look at the animal and know what to do next. **Book Three: The American Venison Cookbook (234 pages)** 70 recipes, 30 for the campfire and 40 for the kitchen. Dutch-oven suppers with real briquette counts. Night-of-the-kill tenderloin over coals. A thermometer number on every recipe. Because meat your kids won’t eat doesn’t feed anyone. **Plus: The Skinner’s Knife Duo** A two-piece bone-handle hunting knife set: a gut-hook blade that zips the hide open without puncturing the gut, and a Persian-style skinner for peeling hide and breaking down the quarters. 3.5" polished stainless blades, natural bone handles, full-grain leather belt sheath that carries both. The two knives you’ll need in your hand the moment the animal is on the ground. Here is what is coming to your door: **The American Deer Hunting Handbook ($19.99)** **The American Deer Skinning Handbook ($19.99)** **The American Venison Cookbook ($17.99)** **Two-Piece Bone-Handle Skinning Knife Set ($69.99)** **Full-Grain Leather Belt Sheath (Included)** **Total Retail Value: $127.96** **Today’s Price: $99.99** You can stock all the ammo, water and freeze-dried food you want. None of it makes you self-sufficient. The man who can walk into the woods and come back with 50 pounds of meat is. These are paperbacks, not PDFs. 714 pages, 48 diagrams, every claim sourced. They go on the shelf next to your other survival manuals and they work when the power doesn’t. This is a limited run. When the knife sets are gone, the bundle comes down. [Get the Deer Hunter’s Bundle for $99.99](https://links.tacticalusa.com/a/1534/click/7568/11767687/6bc36d74e377fce4b96152017f97592d3971ad7a/e2cb5c80fa232a5db0d83b0ecb67642c9fc1f721) Stay safe,

Pat
**Tactical USA** P.S. Even if you've never hunted a day in your life, put this bundle on the shelf for the day you have to. You have 60 days to read every page and handle the knives. If it isn’t the most useful thing in your survival library, send it back for a full refund. [>> Get the Complete Hunter’s Bundle before the run sells out](https://links.tacticalusa.com/a/1534/click/7568/11767687/6bc36d74e377fce4b96152017f97592d3971ad7a/e2cb5c80fa232a5db0d83b0ecb67642c9fc1f721)

body:
The impact we have in 2027 and beyond is going to be directly impacted by what we’re able to raise now.
#

Team --
We’ve got good news and bad news for you.
Good news first: After one of the most successful elections in the history of this organization, a gun safety majority is going to take office in Congress next year. Governors and state legislatures flipped around the country, too.
The opportunity we have to make progress on life-saving legislation is almost unprecedented.
But here’s the bad news: Our fundraising has slowed down, and not by a little.
We know that’s not what you want to hear, especially with Thanksgiving right around the corner. It’s true, though, and it’s actually a bit worse than all that. Because of the holiday, we’re expecting our fundraising to decline even further next week.
That means it is especially important that we make some progress now, before folks begin to take (much deserved) time off with their families. The impact we have in 2027 and beyond is going to be directly impacted by what we’re able to raise now. If we fall short, we lose our edge.
So, to everyone who understands the important role GIFFORDS plays in the fight to keep our families and communities safe, we’re humbly asking:
[**Please, make a donation to GIFFORDS PAC today to help Gabby raise the resources she’ll need to take these fights on — and win.**](https://go.giffords.org/go/14457?c0=giff-em-q42026.PjNIJI&refcode=em261119-1-b&t=1&akid=12088%2E3935704%2E-VN9C7)

That means it is especially important that we make some progress now, before folks begin to take (much deserved) time off with their families. The impact we have in 2027 and beyond is going to be directly impacted by what we’re able to raise now. If we fall short, we lose our edge. ## Foot of Rain Shuts Broward Schools Again
Broward County Public Schools are [closed for a second straight day](https://email.editor.joinflyoverflorida.com/c/eJykkL-OtSAUxJ8GOwzgH7Sg-Bq7-7VbmiOgng16DHAv8e037itsO5OZzPy-XvMLMOC5_YfDm5XW-fQlBZ-zj3MEPAudeSMocMPlr8vHC4OflVA9l5LLcQab8ePnFipndDuAWCpvpB47MXRa62o3yonOKvCLHNZWAHQDNIPWFhrtdC-bCs3TJ6Ucpeh62dWNkItXolvaXowWBtYK7zBTrL8JzzXc9PFxDRTRQW3pqILZc74Sa_4xNTE1lVJqu6Tny-MzNR0IBzI1PRJT0xKpQHTc0vvMN092JwqJ20DJO573d0wObr4GIofnxpd34s5flJ9wFY27CoaAqdesFdsBGH535D8i_Bj1EwAA__-XM4jK) after a foot or more of rain swamped parts of the county on Tuesday night and Wednesday. Superintendent Howard Hepburn said floodwater cut off two bus depots serving thousands of students. The heaviest rain fell on Davie and Hollywood, where [totals topped 12 inches](https://email.editor.joinflyoverflorida.com/c/eJykkLGOtCAUhZ8GOyaAIENB8Td087dbmjty1btBMchqfPuNm32Dbc9JvpPvfLz6F1CidfoPC_oxj_2K556wVix9AVrPvNYpwwkXbLhtWDZK2CuhOi4ll66HodKBvYYmequfIN4NemmdEU9jrW1mj0pqZ-TgulZHa6JTbozGWA3tCG1rG_I3T0rppDCdNI9WyDcqYd66E26AJ9MCI9VcHp-Z1jFd-cAyplwowmPIS5P8XOu2s_YfU4GpcO7HehdMhduHqZDyAImpsBAsxCNEZCrs-avO_BfEZ4Tj4rf0HeXIIR6053IxFZri43ZSSrR3lmkxLUDpZ7r-8bXDq-8AAAD__5GDgl4). In Hollywood, water reached the front doors of several homes and part of Temple Sinai's roof gave way, though no one was hurt. The city and Broward County have declared states of emergency. The National Weather Service estimated [8 to 10 inches fell in three hours](https://email.editor.joinflyoverflorida.com/c/eJykkD2O5CAUhE-DMyzAP-CAYBNnvemG1jM8t98KGwuYRn37kTuZA0z6qapU-v49lgdQoPP5Fw60W9yWE2sOWAqmJQGdNZ7lGaHCGy68LkwXBVyUUCOXkstpAVfohUsPjbe6NyDWBq3U0yDMoLVudtsbMwqnccXOCK-dcdI714_oUEohTEP23pNSTlIMoxzaTsgVlRjWfhSTA8N6gZ5KTO3_SOcW3vGFaQsxkYfWxaMJdi_lyqz7w9TM1Fxrbc_VHQQH3YEbIZQdE1NzLjERZv5DthCj5xWK2_maYoXk-afLPXjklGOAgp7nK5bMXfwKnmdELgWn0-2Y-a2KqbkzZpLCMDU3yfqrUgiUR8168TyAwudr-aXml1XfAQAA__8qupPX) across parts of Broward. A flood watch covers Miami-Dade, Broward, and parts of Palm Beach County through this evening, with drier skies expected into the weekend.

## Florida DMV System Stumbles Again
A computer failure [disrupted driver license and vehicle services](https://email.editor.joinflyoverflorida.com/c/eJykkL2upSAUhZ8GOwxs_6CgmMbuTDulQdwe9wTBACM5bz_x5r7B7df6stb357W8LHkK79_2RLPHfQlYs8dSMC3JUqgxlHe01X7shdeF6SKPCwgYuZRc6sW6QjcuvW02M_XKirVBIyc9CDVM09QcBjYxOrmvelQwaOh3J0e1q1UKgM5J3ZB5eFJKLcUwyqHthFwRxLD2o9DOKtYL3KjE1P6NFHb_iTem3cdEm21dPBtvjlKuzLpfDGYGc621Das7yZ70BBjMzy8Gs4_Oegbzd5snvGIqmVPO_zDzSuXg5UC-JboxZe7JYcjI8ycXPLkNG7_xIOeRZ0w3OXyonVJawcRgbpLZrkreUx4n1ov3acl_bSw_1Hsb-B8AAP__95eRDw) across Florida on Wednesday, after the Florida Department of Highway Safety and Motor Vehicles reported trouble shortly after 11 a.m. The problem hit ORION, the [statewide system county tax collectors](https://email.editor.joinflyoverflorida.com/c/eJykkLGO3CAQhp8Gd6yAxQYXFGncXdqU1iwMvjlhsIDYt28fOcobpBlppNH3zf__-lg_gBLl7Sfs6GKJa8arJewd61qB8lVy3wpc8IYDjwPrQQlXJdTEpeRyXsF3OnHVMARntAXxGtBJM4_CjsaY4dOF6Sm8sVFbaydtRhNmETxKI71RMZqB3M2TUs5SjJMcH08hX6jE-NKTmD1YpgUG6qU-vgrlmN7lxBpTqRTg4cs-JPfZ-9HY8wdTC1PLdV2PO4j-gu_7gKnlXplaUvGQmFpuI1OLlPewTC3_cDzsJ8fvAyth9th4w3qSR15-d9iQQ4zoO-WNh0on1sYTecwNG6_oSw28vVvH2zhUF46LUqI2GabFtgOlv-_2_2z6dOpPAAAA__9A25RH) and state service centers use to process licenses, titles, registrations, and plates. By early afternoon, the agency said it had found the issue and was working to restore service, but it gave no cause or timeline. It's not ORION's first stumble. The system [launched earlier this year](https://email.editor.joinflyoverflorida.com/c/eJykULuu4yAQ_RrcEQHXGLtwsY27u-2W1sQMzqywQTAJm79fOb9wuyOdp86f7_UbKNK5_4YD55DCemKrEZmxrAXobOnkPUGDN2TMGUumiKtRZpBaSz2tsDG9cO2h87PrR1D3DmftJqtG65zrHrNzwVtwwQ3K-956uBvt9QSj2bwPwXY0X3la60krO2h7-1L6jkbZez-oaYNR9Ao9cSq3v4nOEN_phSXEVMjDbUtHF-cHc67i65cwizBLa-12vOvz3BJUviTCLFeJMIuyFx6FWRj-yS3FiBunIlMItGGVBXMqLNO5Jzp3Wd-V8ZBU6xOr9FTLM_OHwPL6GCoDYyOPwixdmX1uFCPVwYle7QdQ_EzkH777ms3_AAAA__-BjZJT), and tax collectors reported repeated outages and slowdowns this spring, with Manatee County logging 12 disruptions in May alone. If a tax collector visit is on your list, check your county's website before heading out.

The seat [opened after Republican state Sen. Brent Taylor won](https://email.editor.thetennesseeflyover.com/c/eJykkL1uhDAQhJ8GOp-8xvy4cJGG7tKmRItZgyNjkL13p7x9dJcoL5B2NJpP33xcpyuGGNL6jjtZZj8lepRIzJSnNROlUighk8P9xLCmcqKjSUnVCQABZkLH4U6TxnqxswKD2tVkoTetHLoWdL3ZVlPrnJn14jygp1n1EkzfNAS9lL6vg30OAoABkEOjLojkB9XNMDjZLbOvtKQl8JEvvBFTSlQKkY9fx53yxR17He3GfJaqeavUWKnxqeE2TImieRZ-o0qN8XAYKzV-Us5BvBwFpnTckqMi8i0Jf2TxBxE__qIQcp3tcj5CjKF0faXlumOILzz_87u7Vd8BAAD__4hMhsc) Tennessee's 9th Congressional District, and it covers parts of Memphis and Shelby County. A date for the special election hasn't been set, and Green said there's a [short timeframe to organize a campaign](https://email.editor.thetennesseeflyover.com/c/eJyk0LGO8yAQBOCnwZ0j74ZgKCj-xl3-9kprjReHEwYLSHL39qfkHuHqkWb0zcd1vlKIIW3_aWfbmp8TP2vk1rjMW2FOtXKixo72g8KW6kGOZxxQ9QA9mJlcCw-eJXWrXRAMSdexhdFcBq0uILub1U7hAmZVhkY_IGk1erkYRLlqGvWlC_ZVCAAGYNBnPBGx16gW0G5Q6-KFHHgNLZdTu3HjlLhWZh-_84PLyeW9i_bW2lHF-Z_ASeDk8xeMr0Tg9CIJnGJ2FAVOn1xK6N-4nlLK9-S49uWeep9L_8vtil2PZ4gxVDUKOWw7hfgean986WHxJwAA__9Ldn1k) in a district Taylor won with 66% of the vote in 2022.

The City of Charlotte has [_moved to dismiss_](https://email.editor.flyovernorthcarolina.com/c/eJyk0D2OpDAUBODTQGbkHzAQONiErDfdED3sR2OtsZH9aKbn9CNGmhNMXFKpvvr3mB_gg4_Pv7CjWaOdI14lIBHm-RPySeU_lNPTeTggtAkKQZgll5oJwcQ4HzmVAy3Nonam75UeXY1G9GPHB93Jsd5Mx_milFWIi-3EqttOD3ZB7OSq0FqsvbkLhRCjEHxox0a73kklkA9WW6XWquXoPKXcrOGdXphjyrRZyCn4CI1Nex3MRnSUSv2p5FTJ6bquZk0fN-fOKzmdpZKT3SCHRITsgkiF-fyOwH6kbD-zw8wCXDeaUSoFHSvwLsxCJLZhcCxjOVIsfglYZ-OOy4fgi-6rlj938OF7D_32zZeRXwEAAP__QX2QAQ) a wrongful-death lawsuit filed by the family of Iryna Zarutska, the 23-year-old Ukrainian refugee stabbed to death on a Charlotte Area Transit System light-rail train in August 2025. In a filing this week, the city [_argues governmental immunity_](https://email.editor.flyovernorthcarolina.com/c/eJykkL2upSAUhZ8GO4wbPSAFxTR2Z9opzRbwSAbFwFbjPP3Em9wnuM1qVrJ-vj_v8Y0hhu3zG1dv5s2Om79K9EQ-j_8wH1T-YjkCHbtD8jZhIYyjaITkABz0uOdUdm9phMoZpVqpXeUNKP1qevkSulqMRWllI149TLZrsevAKtBK6n6eZQuiCuYJBAAN0PSdrqVTTrTgm95K27Yz6xrvAqVcz_FOp89byrRYzCmGDWub1iqahWgvrP3FxMDEcF1XfU10PiYTw1PAxADwiGJisIFubhfMMRF5vqbTF-5CWUMpPOL1nOZTTsdnIT7dfMY1xJuHfG_Iv8kwMVTZuP0KMYYiFeuaz4ohfi2in_I8jfgfAAD__7hijAk) shields decisions about transit policing, security staffing, and public safety from liability under North Carolina law. Zarutska’s family sued the city and its private security contractor in August, alleging inadequate security and weak fare enforcement, including no turnstiles or guards, left riders vulnerable. Surveillance video showed Decarlos Brown Jr., who is charged in her killing, attack her about four minutes after she boarded. The city contends Brown alone is responsible and that the attack could not have been predicted. Charlotte acknowledges [_no security guard_](https://email.editor.flyovernorthcarolina.com/c/eJykkLGuozAQRb_GdEbYEBsKF9vQZdst0aw9BCsGI88kVvbrV4ne-4JXXl3pXp3z57pcIaZ43H7Djm49_HJgpYTMWJZ_UB5Md6BH5McZgNFnIIa06E4bqZRU03KWTCd6XlQTnLW9mUKDTtnp0o3moqdmc50H1EENFqwd1DAaH3q8gPb-bxhw7Zvo3oNKqUmpbhym1gQbdK-wG73xfb-KocMQOZd2Ta_8xHLkwpuHklM8oPV5b5LbmE8S_S-hZ6HnWmtb6fyUQs9vLKFnYmCUX8FvUFJmRkmId5IJ6htVhkh7JIIkY3kdIL89CD03xYWzxpQiGSuG7rZDTJ9__qm9p9P_AwAA__-ZK4ik) was present in the car and that the system lacks fare gates, but denies those factors caused the death. A judge has not yet ruled on the motion.

In a filing this week, the city shields decisions about transit policing, security staffing, and public safety from liability under North Carolina law. Zarutska’s family sued the city and its private security contractor in August, alleging inadequate security and weak fare enforcement, including no turnstiles or guards, left riders vulnerable. Surveillance video showed Decarlos Brown Jr., who is charged in her killing, attack her about four minutes after she boarded. The city contends Brown alone is responsible and that the attack could not have been predicted. Charlotte acknowledges was present in the car and that the system lacks fare gates, but denies those factors caused the death. A judge has not yet ruled on the motion. NC Awards $311M in School Grants Seven North Carolina school districts will split nearly to build and renovate schools, the Department of Public Instruction announced Tuesday. The money comes from the , created in 2017 for economically distressed counties. This year’s total is down about 21% from the $392 million awarded last year. Bertie, Hoke, and Wayne counties and Clinton City Schools each get $42 million for a new elementary school. Lee County receives $52 million for a middle school, Elizabeth City-Pasquotank gets $62 million to construct a new Northeastern High, and Wilkes County receives $28.9 million for Mountain View Elementary. The awards cover only about one in every six dollars districts statewide requested. A recent state survey pegged building needs at . Meanwhile, NCDOT crews are racing to finish emergency sandbag work along a vulnerable 1,600-foot stretch of Highway 12 on Pea Island. ## Lieuwen Tapped to Lead Georgia Tech
The University System of Georgia's Board of Regents on Tuesday [named](https://email.editor.thegeorgiaflyover.com/c/eJykkDFuhDAQRU9jOlYer8FQuEhDt2lTogEPxpKxkT27q9w-IsoN0vzq6z3pfT3mB4YYkv_Egyz7bU70rpGYqcx7rmdgjL6go3p6rIQ1J0qzkqpvAVoY57PketLKMzTO3qUj0ENDFszYyaE3AM1uB9CmX-WwKaOXVaHBTsvR6aUfVt0t1AR7EQFgBADo4NbL8e5cZxZQQK5TQktygXO58U6ecvEBt_idX1Ruaz6aaHfms4r7h1CTUFPJT7-7ghsjR0yM10uo6dIINQFcY4SaYqDnm1Kb8CDX_pFbpnVvt5AwhspCTU2x7nyHGEPtjdDSHxjir5j_G-1l1U8AAAD___NCgOs) interim president Tim Lieuwen the sole finalist for Georgia Tech's presidency. Lieuwen, a Georgia Tech alum who has led the school on [an interim basis](https://email.editor.thegeorgiaflyover.com/c/eJyk0EHK2zAUBODTyDsbPTmWfi-0-NOiFkICXZTQbIwsvdgCWTLSI6a3Lym9QdcDHzNzv05XG2JIy81uqGl5TgmPGpEIy7TmugeycSnWY90XW9HWnDBNggvZArQwTnvJdUdHEzRe99wjnD4a1KDGgX9IBdCs-jk4r3jvFHo1SC6HWSmcXT-ODrmaoQn6LQLACAAwQCf52Hs_qBkEoB8EO3H0gXLpaMUFc1mCfcbf-YWlc3lrol6J9sr6TyYME-Y4ju6oM73eKRPmvYoJE7OzkQljKdpElgnzz2oJ3domu2FtQyIsYWv3gjV4TMSE-SbvX5Uwtx-Pz4s53-Xl_PP7r7P48rgyYZqi_X6EGEOVip34stkQ_9ai_730pcWfAAAA__9WmIt7) since Nov. 1, previously oversaw its research enterprise of more than $1.4 billion a year. During his more than 25-year career at the school, he's also served as executive director of the Strategic Energy Institute and as an expert in clean energy, propulsion, and national security. Pending a final board vote, Lieuwen will succeed Ángel Cabrera, whose [seven-year tenure](https://email.editor.thegeorgiaflyover.com/c/eJykkLGunTAQRL_GdEZeAwYKF2noXtqUaMF7jSVf27I3F-XvI6L8wWtnpKOZ8-tr_8IQQ_I_8U2W_WtPdLdIzFT3K7cSGKOv6KgVj42w5URp10obCSBh3UvNrdDJO3TODsoRjEtHFuZ1UouZAbrLOqXUMBqjyCw0mkFPC7rJHXSqZZ0P6oJ9iACwAgBM0Bu1Ds5N8wEayE1ajIpc4Fx7vshTrj7gK_7JH6r9md9dtBdzaWL4IfQm9Hbfd38e7Tnz9EJvyBETo9DbEwq9_adIpvOSpVILjhJLTJ6iPPGoVFE2plJC8tLlO0nOMhI6mXIqNb8CS2yFkgypceDfTEJvXbWu3CHG0MwsRuXfGOK_jfxdvx-r_wYAAP__BiWTyA) saw enrollment increase by 55% before he left to lead the Aspen Institute.
## Auto Supplier Picks Candler County
Auto parts maker HDI America [announced](https://email.editor.thegeorgiaflyover.com/c/eJykkL2upDAMhZ8mdEGx-RsKim3oZtstkSEGsgokSqzhzttfMbpvcFt_tny-8-85Pcl5d25_6eBBtnU6-cqeRThNe8jRCfktkeUcN8pMOZx8Tmiw1QAa-immkCMvMkFhh8pYhvpR8ABd35hH2wEU-4AGTT8vbb-adYa1wZb6iitG4mZhMoW7V1oA6AEAGihb01fWNt0MCGwbVLVh6ySkUnbeOKTN0erf4cWpXMJR-GEXiVlVfxSOCsfrusplzrfMzRWOJJ5OIYXjPVQ47tZpOji5hXT0dGZdd_pw3rtw6p8XHyCav27DrCVoslbDo9H_w5z1_NZoKqNwLNJg43Uf57ZTtdkOcv6TTH7b6mvA7wAAAP__eaSNdw) plans to build a $47 million plant in Candler County, creating at least 185 jobs by 2030. The roughly 175,000-square-foot facility will [make](https://email.editor.thegeorgiaflyover.com/c/eJykkL2upDAMhZ8mdEGx-RsKim3oZtstkSEGsgokSqzhzttfMbpvcFt_tny-8-85Pcl5d25_6eBBtnU6-cqeRThNe8jRCfktkeUcN8pMOZx8Tmiw1QAa-immkCMvMkFhh8pYhvpR8ABd35hH2wEU-4AGTT8vbb-adYa1wZb6iitG4mZhMoW7V1oA6AEAGihb01fWNt0MCGwbVLVh6ySkUnbeOKTN0erf4cWpXMJR-GEXiVlVfxSOCsfrusplzrfMzRWOJJ5OIYXjPVQ47tZpOji5hXT0dGZdd_pw3rtw6p8XHyCav27DrCVoslbDo9H_w5z1_NZoKqNwLNJg43Uf57ZTtdkOcv6TTH7b6mvA7wAAAP__eaSNdw) automotive seating parts, including seat cushions, headrests, and armrests, and should be fully operational in 2028. HDI America CEO Seung Yong Park cited the site's location, access to major automakers, and support from state and local partners. ## ICE Arrest Practices Challenged in Court
A class-action lawsuit filed Nov. 16 in federal court in Alexandria accuses ICE of arresting people across Virginia without [_warrants or the probable cause_](https://email.editor.thevirginiaflyover.com/c/eJykkLGOrDAMRb8mdBnFgQRSpHgN3bx2S-QhhrGUAZRkg-bvV-xqv2ArF8f20b0f9-mOHHlb_-OLfKnLtNGZI5VCaeKZMCXK5Ug4F54pb1jfZU-TVtpKAAluukilqcMm-AU7QteQh94ZNdje9M3TG9upNjhjrBnAmQWJghtoRudcax-qYX_9AwAHALo1t1aHBdpgVRt65YZBdIoClz3dypMqp5U3xiW-90rpNu-vJvpnKUcW7T-hR6HHs-zHBYQef9eFHi-L0COA0GPEM39ykRgjrZQlXxOj_Amc5eMteSbJm6zXaZN8OE6OkbPtRafWF3L8Vpc_tla9_goAAP__fuaBeg) federal law requires. The ACLU of Virginia, the Legal Aid Justice Center, the Washington Lawyers’ Committee, and the law firms Bailey & Glasser and Covington & Burling [filed it on behalf](https://email.editor.thevirginiaflyover.com/c/eJykkL3OnDAQRZ8GOiP_sBgXLtLQfWlTosEeYCSvWdmzkH37iERRHiD1Pbo6Oj--5i-gRHn7Dk_0fK5zxqsmZMYyU0AoBSu_CgSmgDXD-eGjzFrqQSgllJvv5cS5hzb6FXoE16JX1j3kONiHbXc_LgYcmCUMEkbUblmUtW4Y1GitldK05O8_pZRTSmnz6IyOqzJxkCZa6cax6SVG4qN0vONJZaNMsKbPcWLpwvFsk9-ZX7Ux3xo9NXq6rquDhD8hx0KwFML15ho9hQS1ilv6yGKlhFFQFv9YsWLEAkmE411YVPhUQQEFVfGnBeVN_FXIVVzE-_FmcUEpkLk2emqLj6-LUqI62KaX2xMo_dbk_yx8ev0rAAD__4wSlTQ) of six Virginia residents and the Centreville Immigration Forum, a nonprofit. Defendants include the Department of Homeland Security and Secretary Markwayne Mullin. Federal law allows [_warrantless immigration arrests_](https://email.editor.thevirginiaflyover.com/c/eJykkLGupTAMRL8mdEFJ4AIpUmxD97bdEnkTX7AUAnL8QPfvV-wvvMaSNdLMnPnztXwBZSrrb9gxyPVeCt41owjyQhGBGaucDFEoYi1wfeTgxRk3aGu19cujXLj00KTwhh7BNxjs6F9mGsbX2GwBjOmmyU_RT2MajBsQY8LBOB-9T25qKDx-1lpvrXXdq-1cetsuDaZLo_HTpHqDieTgVja8iFcqBO_8OS7kNh57k8MmclbV_VJuVm6-77tNW23X41JufpCUm58Q5WbjntMrN6et6opSNWM8OOkqDLRuoiHtVOh5HzZ9AzMUqRpK0rAjU4Siz--_maKu3-d5sDQc0nlTzlSHUfVm3YHy_27yw1mv4P4FAAD__zigjnc) only when officers have probable cause to believe a person is in the country illegally and likely to flee before a warrant can be obtained. The suit says ICE skips that assessment and claims more than half of the people ICE arrested nationwide in July 2026 had no criminal record. DHS [_disputed claims_](https://email.editor.thevirginiaflyover.com/c/eJykkL2OoCAUhZ8GOw1c_IGCYhu72XZLw8BVb4Jo4I5m3n7j7iNM_Z2cnO_8-Vg-PCXK229_oON7XTI-NSEzloUC-lKw8lV8YApYs7-_-SwLSBhbpVpll5fcuPS-iW71PXrboFOTHaQZp2FqdgfGgOqlAruClNOodQyfk4V1HHQ0q2nIvX1KKauUAj10GuKqdByljpO0xoheYiQ-S8c73lQ2yuTX9H3eWLpwHk1yO_NVhf4lYBYwP8_T5c_w-LpT3vjMb0rA_MoJmK-ClSJmbrl8HVd7nYmYwouSf-oXcUsB2__ytY1BwNxLZbSyAuamuHg9lBLVcRK93A5P6d8M_uGDt4O_AQAA__8Fz4ZN) of indiscriminate arrests, saying its operations are targeted.
## Federal Grant Funds Mine Communication Research
A Lynchburg company and Virginia Tech are part of a $24 million project, backed by $17.7 million in proposed federal funding, to [_build wireless networks_](https://email.editor.thevirginiaflyover.com/c/eJykkbHOpDAMhJ8GOq9IgAUKimvo_muvRN7EgPWHZOV4We3bn_JL9wTXWLLm09ij-fO1fiEHjvtvPGnWa1sjvXMgVZKVHaEIZX0KOmVHOeL10SSrbewdjAEzrUW5aO2w9vOGHeFU02yGqW_G-9AP9TE_aBiaR9-Ydmp9h35ypnVb3_fGj36yW81z8TPGTMYY2_a31vrNtP7etH5opnGsuoY8a5KbHnSx7BwZt_BJF8nNpbMO86H6zFX7q7JLZReH4jliKGFuSfbKLuVEZRdjyhgLkzDAyZEyoBAE_iZ4RU-yS3pFD46VKRfilUEoMD4CwZuFAuUMkfSd5LtImVDcQZIBFf69B0ru-HEuGMcdUgQ-n5Kusrh0nq_IDpVTBIweMm6kn8outcz--eYQON-Hqmv2Ezn8xNT_bOia7d8AAAD__3rlq34) that reach the deepest parts of mines. Innovative Wireless Technologies leads one of four projects the Department of Energy selected for its [$73 million “Mine of the Future” initiative](https://email.editor.thevirginiaflyover.com/c/eJykkLGupiAQhZ8GO4yAihQU29jdbbc0c2XUSRANjBrffvPffYStz5eTc74_X9MXUKS0_oYdPd_LlPApEZkxTzQj5IyFzwwz04wlwf3ykSfd6F4qJZWbPsmNUwtV8Au0CK5Cr6zrmqG3na02b3XvbAdoXBdgbgcTrA26b4xtQfffriL_6VNKOaWUNl1tdFiUCX1jgm3cMIi2wUB85Jo3vCmvlAiW-B435no-9ir6jfkswvwSehR6fJ6nxoR5fev1uIUetxUPoUfITHPEIvR4FRnwhMw7Jpb_YBnhSvOGRe6UUC4XXxklJWKCz8siv49YGLO8fhBKq6QUrsL5rbIP50MxUumtaJt1B4o_4_g_vd5e_w0AAP__qUaRrQ); awards are still being negotiated. Virginia Tech expects about $4.6 million. In a deep mine, a dropped signal can hide an injured worker, a gas buildup, or a failing machine. The team will test 5G-based networks at the Virginia Tech Quarry and the university’s autonomous mining lab, with [_partners including_](https://email.editor.thevirginiaflyover.com/c/eJykkL-OrSAQh58GOw2DiFJQ3Mbu3HZLQ2BUEhQDczTn7Tdstf12M_l9-ebP12t52RDDuf23Bxq61-XEp0QkwrwEhzZnLHRl6yg4LKe9P5TyIrhQLUALeqnJjYu0jTerlWh1gwZGPfBJjcPY7EYqjkoPtgeHWvfWKQ5CSAQ3yQnV0ARTfQCgAUD0Q9cLv0LvFe_9yPU0McnRB0q5ox3vkLdwBrvGT7oxdy4dTTQ70VVY_4-JmYn5eZ7uQLKR0O31okoxMRdK-cPEXOcxMXPNxAy1OsIZzq2tOBOzT9iW93WlTKX9FbVXTndttpzepy_VpOXY7XTEJht_PSHGUNTIJN8OG-LPcvTHv95GfAcAAP__JTmNJQ) the Colorado School of Mines, the University of Kentucky, and a training center in West Virginia.
## Navy To Retire Its Iconic Peacoat
The Navy, whose largest base is in Norfolk, will [_end authorized wear_](https://email.editor.thevirginiaflyover.com/c/eJykkD1uhDAQRk9jOiPGBoMLF2noNm1KNNgDa4k_2bOs9vaRc4U00zzpad7385geGLd4rN-4k-N7mQ56542YKU3RE6ZEma-EnqOnfOD94TNNqlFGAkiwUyE3TS1WwS3YEtqKHPS2awbTd331dNYQtFqZ2WroBzubeaHQkremU2awcxVd8QGABQClu1qrsIAOptGhb-wwiLahEPlMNT_pjmmNR8Rl-5w3pdqfe7W5J_OVhf4SahRqLBH1Kx-xPtMq1Fj8Qo0A5WihxovQn8iS7uiZglzSuctSJzOhnHHNEhemJFF6OviVPhK5sCq5cL3jtsVsetE2645x-_uB_znf7dRvAAAA___JNYRt) of its wool peacoat on Oct. 1, 2027, closing a run that dates back to the 1886 uniform regulations. Sailors will use a synthetic cold-weather parka instead. The policy, released Nov. 13, also [retires the acrylic V-neck sweater](https://email.editor.thevirginiaflyover.com/c/eJykkD3OpDAQRE8DmRE2vw4cbEI2m26IWnYztGRs1O6Bnduv2Ct8cZVK9d6f1_oCipTev-FAJ9e2JrxLRBHklTwCMxY5GbyQx5Lg-krm1bRmVForbdcnuXDtoQ5ugx7B1uj0ZId2HqdhqncHwQ_a62mwxg8zop1xRhMGY8feYtfW5J49rbXVWptuaDoTNt2Fse3C1Np5rvoWA0nmRna8iN-UCLb4zRdy4_NRR7eLnKXqflVmqcxy33cT6cKU7y3_fSqVWR6yyiyfoh4MxSjEqEiKIp8TeXUi-AyiYBNkdWRGJTsk5THJh7-qINTswnlTjFTGqerb9wEU_1-QH9q7nPkXAAD__49_h6s) and the dinner dress white jacket. The dinner dress blue jacket becomes the year-round formal option, and the wool V-neck stays. One change comes much sooner: the desert-camouflage Navy Working Uniform Type II can’t be worn after Nov. 30. The same order replaces the gold-and-blue PT uniform with an all-blue Improved Physical Training Uniform, which joins the seabag Oct. 1, 2027. Vice Adm. Jeffrey Czerewko, chief of naval personnel, [_issued the policy_](https://email.editor.thevirginiaflyover.com/c/eJykkM9qhDAQxp8m3laSUePmkMNCEXpw6ak9ymhGHYh_SIKyb19s-wY9zW8YmO_H99V2LbLndXriQjYdY7fSGT2lRKHjgTAEimkPOCQeKK54vNIWOpCgb0rdlOmuy0FdiZmzI5aEJiOralPJu66rOptt3_dDr9CQJIAK0JAikg7LUutBQ5Gxvf4ppYxSCooqL8CNqnBaFq6W5n4XpSTHaQt5mungMPHKOPrXdlDIh23JvJ1T2qMoHgIaAc15nvnyumznkF8jX9gLaD62kNBHAU1VCWhaihEnuvbn4_Px1r4_f_Hy-SMNtcx3N2bBuv1k7znqWpRyWpD9T3j6Z2-Hhe8AAAD__5QbgJ0), which follows Chief of Naval Operations Adm. Daryl Caudle’s push to simplify uniforms and shrink the seabag.

## Xi Greets Trump With Tarmac Hug
Chinese President Xi Jinping broke protocol yesterday and met President Trump at the bottom of Air Force One's stairs in Shenzhen, China, with a handshake and a hug. [See photos here](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJyk0D1ywyAQQOHToM4edgEhCoo0mjRO61Kjn0Uig4wH1rJz-4xzhbSv-Ip3vQyXMaZ4W7_GnTyHPNzoWRMxUxlecS1EXLk89vucK8-ZdiorDSixPQGcwA3jzPGgAZrFByIk1ZAH64zsrLNds3ln3DRNVndhaqcOiAw47MzYBimNcUsT_ZsDAAeg0JgzarMsc7ABZSulmoWWtETO5fyd4403CuknH1TOc96b5DfmexXqQ2AvsH-9q8D-ukWmz_yoJLCvPPKjCuwRUEl0CrRtje40KGiKX-7PmFKsrRVarvsY0x_N_xtyePwNAAD__9BMck4). The gesture [returned the welcome](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJykkD3OpDAQRE9jMpC7-XXgYBOy2XRD5DFt6JXByPQMs7dfMVf4kkpKeqV6fx7Tw3HkffntNrIS0rTTdUYSoTx9eMlEckp-bYdPp_hEG-WFJtTYlQAlmMl54TdNUMw2ECHVBVnoTauH3vRDsVr_HFpEE7rBBzTom7lx9fAkcL0hdG3B9sYBgAGosW0rbNp59qEPqDuta68aTTNLytXfxLusFOK_9KZc-bQV0a4ix6nqXwpHheN1XZX7cDrvVuF4sxWOAHcMCsfvm9KvvLvyw-X6WkrH-UhZimzn4-IY-ex61ehlcxy_I_IzNW-L_wMAAP__KAN3rg) Trump gave Xi at Joint Base Andrews in September. Hours later, Trump shook hands with Russian President Vladimir Putin for the first time since their Alaska summit in August 2025. Putin, who arrived earlier in the day, was greeted by a lower-ranking party official and held talks with Xi for about [two hours](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJykkLGu3CAQRb8Gd6xgjJd14WKjyErz0qRIaSEYL5OHwYLZ9cvfR95fSH2kq3vO74_lw1Gi_PjpNpx4LUvGoyVkxrp80aMicuP63HZfGvuCG9YHLqDgKrWWelycZ3rhorswrYiAfYeTtuOgbna0ty5OxhgbnHI3fTWgDeh1HKzF4P2gjL7ZjqZzTms9at3DMFzADCH41a6grkr1XhiFgbjUy59CmSOu6W95Yb34snVpisx7E_1dwCxgPo7jsrV8MgEzZvlsAubT6oSlpiBgfhvJFt0nNhldDk0exFHuT6YsXQ7yi6SL6IIsq4zUuFTykl36bJKy9JGyEzC7Ku93iD_uLy36uXgKov_-7cyJR_uFde_qFPaDUqJ2tcKox-YovX_z_9V-TfAvAAD__7eylYE) before the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation summit opened. Today, the three leaders hold their first-ever three-way meeting, expected to cover Ukraine, Iran, nuclear arms, trade, and AI chips. Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky has warned against any plan to end the war being discussed without Kyiv or Europe at the table.
## House Democrat Warns GOP Probe Targets
Rep. Robert Garcia, the California Democrat expected to chair the House Oversight Committee in January, sent letters yesterday to [12 people in President Trump's orbit](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJykkLGO3CAURb8Gd4zgeWyPCxcTRURKtGlSpLQIPPCLMIzgrZ39-2jmF7a-0tU55_fb-mYpUY4_7Y4Lh7JmPFtCZqzrP4oVkRvX9_3hSmNXcMcacQUFo9Ra6nm1junAVXd-CYiAfYeLnuZB3aZ5unXb4tQ02sH3Sqk_DsYw4XALHnqYw4zTqDtannda61nrHobhAtfBexemAGpUqnfiqtATl3r5WyjzhiF9lAPrxZW9S8vG_GiivwswAsx5npe95ecmwGCW702AeVoJMIU3rAJMtNWRlZEObPKlJ21KhE2irelDnrZmylGWLHlDSfnAxhQtU8lNcpGu7CjA2Crvd9i-_fieRG-KIy_6r1-eOfFsv7A-urr4x0kpURsncVVxt5Re3Py52scC_wMAAP__2eSWyQ) telling them to preserve documents ahead of planned investigations. The recipients include Donald Trump Jr., Eric Trump, Jared Kushner, Vice President JD Vance, chief of staff Stephen Miller, Attorney General Todd Blanche, and former Homeland Security Secretary Kristi Noem. The [letters outline probes](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJykkTHPnDAMhn8NbD6RcBwwMHS57evaEeUSA66SGDmGr9-_r7hKVfeur18_kh__-Jg_HEXK63eXcNKF54yfJaIqyvyLVkHUonKk3XNRz5hQVpxtYx9gDJhxdl7pxNnUYVoQLbY1TqYfu2box36otwlDeFkMr3a4P7qxd411_YDDsLTt8vJdV9N04YwxozGt7bqbvXch-KVfbPNomtZX9wYDKcvtJ1PWDZf4xSfKzXOq47Sp7qVqv1X2WdnnNSi0bhowsRen5bbxUfC28lnZ53VeZZ-7YCkgGNEVvALKnhPlFf7ug98cSXIZhF8oCqsTTw6iO7LfsEBgfyTMChcM5XRKnOGPuwKc4e0NFpcofoFnkWN_VzzLzuIU_w3DViBR8ZzD4RVcDoB7UaSrf6LAsdcyhf2TYqTy6Kt7syZH8S1B_-9152R_BwAA__9wBbnF) into the family's crypto business, immigration enforcement, and the handling of the Epstein files. The letters [carry no legal force](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJykkDuu5CAQRVdjZ1h8_A0IJnHWk05o0VDGNTLQgmp7ZvdP9FvCy6p0paN77p_H9jB4YvS_TQBNe9oi3OUEIsjbP_QZgArld3jZVMgmCJA9bJLLkQnBxLIZS3jBJlqndwAJqgUtpmXg87RMc3toAIBlHoQUCsZJCbWovld2WGbppON7i7rihBCLEEoOQyf7wTm7T7vkI-fKNj0Hh5Ry9zdhpAP283-6IHc2hfbUB9GrNOpXI9dGrvd9d_ZZqkbNG7nWs5FrTk_IxLzJFg37Vizs48aO9C7AKrOgP4iZ6JivbwwQiWXYUw7MphCQCIBhvKAQekOYYoW3WbvXjeeJZZyanvtg8Pz0o5-temn5FQAA__9fcpDp) until Democrats take the majority. They come days after a U.S. attorney threatened to investigate Garcia for what he called weaponizing congressional oversight.
## Gamers Go Gaga for _Grand Theft Auto VI_
After 13 years and two delays, the _Grand Theft Auto VI_ videogame went on sale at midnight local time around the world, and fans are [going to extremes](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJykkL2u1DAUhJ_G6c4qdn68KVIsQukuEqKgjA72sWNw7Mg-d3PZp0eBR6Cb0Uijme_72_qGIYbkv-BOM7u8JjprJGYq60fwhYgrl_f9MLmyybRT8bSqVo0gJchpRcPhSats7OyIFHUNzVJPQ3vXk7432zyh651Go4zpx-H-Q6NTrtN2GOhO2tkmzFedlHKSslPDcFP9YK1x2ql2bNvOiL4lGziX288cEm_k4u_8pHIzeW_ivDEfVXQPoRahlvM8b3tNVybUQgk-olDL9UqoJfNG5Z-FF2HEZIFLML8qXBJTescIkfBJwBtBpOR5q-AwVcBC4HNIHjiDywU8I4xCLVjg8VDb6-vxEt2STbCi-_zpgkpn_UblaMpsjzPEGOqoRd_6HUP8u57_j_lzVn8CAAD__0uvmUA) to be ready. Some booked the day off, some bought a new console just for the game, and some tricked their consoles into thinking they were in New Zealand, where it unlocked first. Comcast expects the launch to [break its all-time record](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJyk0LEO2yAYBOCnwRsR_GCIB4Yu3tK1o0Xgt0OFIYI_dvP2lfsKnU_6dHe_HsvDp5zK9tPv6GitS8GzZyTCtvxJW0OkTu2zv0PtFCru2DZcQIDhUnI5LT5QOnCRQ3QrIqAa0Ek7jeJuJ3sfXi4-9eQl6GDvxkhttH16u04KQjACpBqSuzgp5SSlgnG8gR5jDKtdQRghVGBaYExU2-13TYVeuOZvPbDdQt2H7F5E787UDwYzg_k8z1sq4coYzM-WfOGhFmrYfGcwb82XyC-EuP9Q5YZv5PmReCqErSDxUPfgO_FcO_F3q_FzbUz05avvlL8M5klqZUdQQ3PxfaacUzeWabHtPuV_vej_3jwc_A0AAP__hqqLLw) for web traffic, and one academic projects $1 billion in lost productivity as players skip work. One U.S. Army unit in Georgia offered soldiers four days off for the game's release if they agreed to re-enlist. The game costs $79.99 and has already [generated $1.5 billion](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJykkD1uxCAUhE-DOyz-bNYFRRp3mzalxcLDJsHGgrdLcvvIuUK6kUYzo_k-7svdxhSP9d3uYDDk5YBWEyBCWb7jWgCwYnnup8sVXYYdygqLYGKknFM-LdZhfMHCO28CgADZgeF6GthNT_rWbYbbKUivwD9AqgcPN6WnwPRoRRgHJ1UXzVXHOZ84l2IYeqEG713QQbCRMemIYuAj5tJ_5njgBiH95BeU3uW9S2ZDPCuRb0TMRMyttd496nXj8omYL0nEvBZ7eHqlkdonZjrSAglsBeotAj1LdEDbZpFipl9HbkTMXTH-bDGlWEdNFFt3G9PfLv6P1suI3wAAAP__ks-Ahw) from nearly 16 million preorders, the most in history, according to one estimate. Critics gave it a 99 out of 100 on Metacritic, tying the record for the highest-rated game ever.

## Clean Harbors Explosion Followed Fires
Harris County fire investigators found evidence of [two minor fires](https://email.editor.thetexasflyover.com/c/eJyk0L2O4yAUBeCnwR0WXPAPBcU27rLtltY1XMdosbEwsZO3HyUazQtMfaSj851_t_GGIYbt_hdXsuU5p3Gj64hUCuXRRcJtwTylfNBzj-kIacOyziMIaLmUXJoRXQknjbLydhLeyIqs7EwjetOqplqs9x2iUS2BnLRxcuqkaJzslVe-xbapgn23SSmNBCGUrp3R2plJYzNR33vNtCAfSsp1WajQE485vtJJuXZpraJdStkPpv4wGBgM13XV_88HvUMGA-YSXCQGwxvGYIjJYWQw_ID4HDLxj5V_Y_mMLsRQXjwi31MuxJf0OEraGAzQNxxmpRvlO44CFNedN7z3CFy2yk0CZ6cUVNn6_QoxhqPtmBb3FUP8TC6_fPq08BUAAP__wFaSaQ) at Clean Harbors' hazardous waste plant near Deer Park in the week before Tuesday night's explosion, a blast that shook homes miles away, sent one worker to the hospital, and heavily damaged a waste-treatment tank. In the earlier fires, flammable vapors escaped from the treatment process before igniting. On Tuesday, they [ignited inside the tank](https://email.editor.thetexasflyover.com/c/eJykkL1uwyAURp_G3rAAYxwGhi7e0rWjxc91jITBgpvYefsqUVV173706Tvn6zpfTYgh3T7NBhrPJc8JjhoBEcrsIpi0mmJzqXDuMdeQk8FtmTnlkjBGmJqNw_CAmbVeW-oVa0GzUQ30omQ_tKu2_SAkjN4pZ510dByNdHLprXVeOuHboF9rjDHFOKW96JwSwikrzGDhcvGiERR8wFw6XAHhNHWJz_yA0rm8tVGviHtt-o-GTw2fjuPolnxyueZ7xZxeUMOnl1bDp2jIngsC-fUh5o5rLgEDVFKg7jn5kG6kwBv0f8h3D_IThCzGhRjw2Rbt9yPEGKocG0FvmwnxfQ3_WfSh-XcAAAD__1v6kXw), despite a pressurized nitrogen system and incinerator line meant to prevent that. Air monitors detected no hazardous levels, and officials issued no shelter-in-place order. County Judge Lina Hidalgo still [called for a thorough review](https://email.editor.thetexasflyover.com/c/eJyk0L1yhCAUBeCn0Q4HEH8oKNLYbdqUzhWuCxMUB-6u7ttnNkVeIP2ZM-d8X7f5BiGG_f4JGxq61jTveJaIRJhnGxF2D3lJueB1xFRC2oG2dZZc9kwIJvQMlsITZ1E7s3CnRY1GDLrjo-7brvZmkXwQ3YKtRqdaO47KjajFwK20EmVfB_NuE0JoITlvVWO1UlYvCroFx9GpSnF0gVJuyCPhBWWNr_TE3Ni01dF4oqNU7Uclp0pO53k2a7pk79OjUNrfoUpO71uVnDzkHAqz6bHTi60hI9sgFw8xMoc2QsbCLDwKsgjsSJmQOcTMDsjf7A-hzsYdZ4gxlH6oFL9vEOLvHPqn4tPInwAAAP__1wWK1w), saying that in another scenario, "this could have been a real big problem." Deer Park said it [was unaware of prior issues](https://email.editor.thetexasflyover.com/c/eJyk0DGu4yAYBODT4A4LMGBTUGzjLttuaf3AT4wWGwuTOHv7VaKnd4FXjzSab_7clhuknPb7b9jQtlcsy47XmbE1rIvPCPsK1ZV64uvI5Uxlh7bFRTChKeeUmwV8S09ceBesY8HwDi0fjWKT0YPqViu548FNYKJQ0QMfvQNulPI4sjCi6pJ9t3HODReMDbL3RkpvnATlcJqCJJJhSK3Uvq3Y8AVnzP_KE2vvy9Zlu7Z2nGT4RcRMxHxdV_93LY93SMQMtSWfkYj5DSNizsVDJmL-4OiXjn7zaEwV6eMI0JCuPm6FiFlMiupoYgDPqddCU8lwoCZoT5kMUujJjcpjV204rpRzOvVIJLtvkPJnZfvhuU8r_gcAAP__2rqOTA) at the plant and is pressing for answers.
## Man Accused of Faking Veteran Status
A 24-year-old San Antonio man is accused of [posing as a veteran](https://email.editor.thetexasflyover.com/c/eJykkD2y4yAQhE8jZeMCjGQTEGzi7G26oWoEwxO1_LhgLOndfsu-wubdX3V_f76WL4wplu_fmMnyGepS6OiJmKktLhGWDdtaW6fzmWqPtSDnsCihZpASpFnQcdxpkaO3q_BGjmTlzUzibubrNG72SmK9rYJI3p0JxiAJo7SYxG2SkyMxRvumSSmNVEJc9cUZrZ1ZNU4r3e9eD1qQj1zbhTdiOrGH9FN3ahdX85jsxvzsw_XXoB6DehzHcQn1VPNWX51reYcG9XjfGtQjkO_wYUDGAgH_koedmBoW6Iz86nDEAhLmDIE8NUzgauGGjjv0mvynBJjzq0SOtcCrA7b8Mzbrn0dMKfb5NmjxnTGmz0T-T7O7Vf8CAAD__6AHkZs) and a military contracting officer to land more than $1.6 million in federal contracts, then supplying the Army with counterfeit ammunition, weapon lights, and rifle optics. Prosecutors say Marcelo Fascino, who never served, passed off his La Vernia company as veteran-owned to win contracts reserved for veterans. He also allegedly [posed as contracting officers](https://email.editor.thetexasflyover.com/c/eJykkbESmzAQRL9GdOdBssCooEhD57QpmUM6QBOh80gXY_99hvxCmm12Znfe7q_n_MSYYt5-4kGjfFaeM501kQiV2SfCvGNZuFT6vBLXyBnlWGfTmh60Bu1m9BLfNOsmjEsbnG5o1A_XtYPr712zjy7cyfnB9gN1nTY4-IcO7qGt74beu6WJ45WmtXbatO3d3ryz1rvFYrfQMASrbEshCpeb7CT0wbqmL7-p3DwfTRp3kVdV9x_KTMpM53nefleUy1RmunCUmRJ7TMpMV5Uyk9aXDMpMFTNgFs6R4cAMMYfohQJwBr9j2agCr_DiGvMGWOGIKQqWL3jOUi76vAGva_RUoFK61gTPf7JQWSkKbIQFhAHL8VVmasoYXmdMKdb-oWy7HRjTPxL5zwPeo_kbAAD__4RenTI) for the Army, Air Force, and other agencies, calling himself "SSG Marcelo Fascino" to prevent rival vendors from bidding. The indictment cites Chinese-made weapon lights passed off as American-made and [a forged letter](https://email.editor.thetexasflyover.com/c/eJykkb2uozAUhJ8GuhPhn8S4oNiG7m67JTrYB7DWP5F9EnLffsW-wi1nRhrNp_nztXxhiCHvvzHRxJ-tLJnOFomZ6uIiYT6wrqU2-jxjaaFk5LQtcpAPEAKEXdBxeNMiej-tg7eip0kYex9G-1D3_pisu4_WoBiM8qOS47pau6JRaJRBZVQfpqtNCGGFHAalb85q7eyq8b7SOHrd6YF84FJvfBDTB9sWv8ub6s2V1MfpYH62Tv3q5NzJ-TzP21_K7X6lnZyxcnCROjlfZJ2cXQ3pkg0zYOaSQ4GEGUL2wTF5OEMl2Cq-PDxLC3mHNzFVzOBK5noB5x3KtgVHFcQjQXMHJQJXXpXBF_dKlLkB1vR9mZmpbhQY9lL8NUEaBUKvo0FjQDzECNpuCuxIBqQmqVYltEbs6-SfZ4gxtIfp9LAnDPE_Nf_wrPck_wUAAP__FRGqqw) from an optics maker. Fascino faces three counts of wire fraud, each carrying up to 30 years in prison, and three counts of false personation of a federal officer, each carrying up to three years.
## Ex-Boxing Champ Held in El Paso

Friend,
Folks are tired of getting ripped off. They are tired of working themselves to the bone and still barely being able to afford their bills.
That frustration lifted my campaign and many other Dems in the Deep South to the top. I finished FIRST in the race for Louisiana’s 5th Congressional District, one of the reddest districts in the country.
Experts said we wouldn't even be competitive, let alone win. _They've never been so out of touch._
[](https://zzejj9hbb.cc.rs6.net/tn.jsp?f=0010IOPuwUyDnhfqk532ULmCJ1VO3Bkg-3r05unpiXg7AKIO-ro0cOyeRRB1Dc_6yMl0AO3ueRKZexWwkhcG46impTdfHxTSDBrp3x1Hp8sWe37SfOd3RTjdTcCKS7VIcw31v6MQr1MlgyHI-xuuaKDwmz8_fus8paInV4RJfBIXgC8WLfbLfTKoOJC-Uim60e4bos3uJCd8TWwPpf0iJE0gTJQkaYrUlcGtxuwrc_b_UoN66bz_i9l5u3nU28yxPEx&c=N0rNfOCSNo7hTncgvRhc0RB2IXBfTQTmPq9CYuwVIyBg8R1uHyn0lg==&ch=JF5PbzN4tn7UoHxyMKGIorKwzTze5ZKyP6uNFnx6ffutpY_mxOnTgA==)
---
**Now I am headed to a December 12 runoff against a MAGA insurance adjuster.**
In the state legislature, my opponent wrote a law that lets insurance companies kick Louisiana homeowners off their policies. Families here already pay some of the highest insurance rates in America. He made it easier to drop them.
I am running to work for the people, _not the big insurance companies._ So they're unloading everything they have to defeat me.
[**I urgently need the support of Dems across the nation to counter their attacks and expose my opponent as the insurance industry puppet he is.** Please, can you rush a contribution of just $3 today to flip a red House seat and prove the experts wrong again?](https://zzejj9hbb.cc.rs6.net/tn.jsp?f=0010IOPuwUyDnhfqk532ULmCJ1VO3Bkg-3r05unpiXg7AKIO-ro0cOyeRRB1Dc_6yMl0AO3ueRKZexWwkhcG46impTdfHxTSDBrp3x1Hp8sWe37SfOd3RTjdTcCKS7VIcw31v6MQr1MlgyHI-xuuaKDwmz8_fus8paInV4RJfBIXgC8WLfbLfTKoOJC-Uim60e4bos3uJCd8TWwPpf0iJE0gTJQkaYrUlcGtxuwrc_b_Up8WXfx43wv0FtFGwXunoKr&c=N0rNfOCSNo7hTncgvRhc0RB2IXBfTQTmPq9CYuwVIyBg8R1uHyn0lg==&ch=JF5PbzN4tn7UoHxyMKGIorKwzTze5ZKyP6uNFnx6ffutpY_mxOnTgA==)

We have to stop the America Last Mob
| This is what happened to America.As we let in tens of millions of foreigners from the Third World into our nation, we have given up our values along the way.As the Third World took over America, one thing became a crime: Pride in America.Our institutions of assimilation have completely turned against us, and now children are taught to hate America because that is somehow morally superior.And the Radical Left was the mastermind of this plot. Now, people won't allow the military to be unapologetically pro-America.And people will revolt if law enforcement puts American citizens first.[We're slowly losing America.](https://trk.email.exclusive-update._UBhnXjPOowA)We used to share the same love for America, and we stood strong together.[Now it is a prerequisite to put America LAST.](https://trk.email.exclusive-update.)But let me tell you: America has given me EVERYTHING, and I can't give up that easily.As a constitutional lawyer, I've fought to protect America's fundamental values. And I'm not stopping the fight. I'm here to tell the Radical Leftists that their Hate America Campaign must end now.

Please step up today for our country.](https://trk.email.exclusive-update.)

**Good Morning!** On this day in 1932, Colorado State University's fight song, the [_Aggie Fight Song_](https://email.editor.thecoloradoflyover.com/c/eJykkLuu2zAMhp9G3mzo4svR4CFo4e106dDRYCTaJiJLgUQnzdJnL-KiT3Am4iPIDz_-X5_zJ1CguP6AHUd2yxzxWQIyY56hFCoMkbd0FCx3hBtmPvJt1lL3tVK1sjM4pgfOLVR-XBbtoK9wVIPtpDVG6mobO9t3xlijPlovh05a6UBqJQ20Sl4HqGh8-5RSVhmpjG389QMXZ9DqxXZD34tWoidOueENXQopg09LeKUH5salvQrjxnwvwlyEnoSetrSjSzvFtXmfFwbGBv0h9MS0Y6CIQk__TTXUe319P2CpXTlOhxHm8keYC-NvFub7ROvGQnda_kxxFfobb3hiyrRShHACH_HfFqI_Z3hlcqXKo78_KQQq_SBaue5A4QzOX-z8Meq_AQAA__8vLpTY), made its debut during a football game against the University of Utah. A turkey named Dolly "Pardon" was among those formally spared from the Thanksgiving table at Colorado's [fourth annual turkey pardon](https://email.editor.thecoloradoflyover.com/c/eJykkL2O6yAQhZ8Gd1gw-CcUFLdxl9tuaY1hHLMhxgISK2-_YqWVtt_2jObo-87Hdb6iD36__ccHmWLXeaczByqF0ow5-1xwL1t8ZsoH4Z1Seab7DAIGLiWXekZb_IvmDhtn1hUsDg0ZOepeaKUENJuxnRArCqdUPzqnBVxcr5cLwtgv5MTYeFP7pJRaKiGVbt1yodUq0rDqfhwG1glyvsTUlo1sDDGhi2t4xxel1sZHE8xWypGZ-sdgYjCd59naJVeXemcw_XwxmGr6K-G3WrPHxD8xkeNHDD7zqklvfmByceeVj8HUJOOO04fg8zCyTtwe6MM3QPnjdi8DXwEAAP__iMiGOw). Find out more below. Your phone is better at protecting you than you think. It just needs permission. Americans reported $7.7 billion in online crime losses last year, and texts are scammers' favorite first move. Some of the strongest defenses sit dormant in your settings. Today, on _The Flyover Podcast,_ Ayla walks through seven settings, most of which take under a minute to turn on. Which one stops a thief who already knows your passcode? And which setting could speak for you when you can't? body:
It’s a tale about what happens when people lose touch with their past.

| | Dear Fellow American, How are you today? Here on campus, it’s not unusual to see students wandering back and forth outside a classroom, practicing before a big test. It reminds me of the story of someone else who wandered around, searching for something he lost... **The Headless Horseman.** According to the legend, this Hessian soldier was decapitated by a cannonball during the Revolutionary War. Gruesome, right? Well, each night, his ghost rides through Sleepy Hollow, searching for his missing head. It’s the unforgettable image at the heart of Washington Irving’s “The Legend of Sleepy Hollow.” But Irving’s story isn’t just a ghost story we tell around Halloween. **It’s a tale about what happens when people lose touch with their past.** The past is old stories, myths, landmarks, and traditions that connect the people of Sleepy Hollow to those who came before them. Irving understood something we desperately need to remember today: **A people who forget the stories that made them will lose the inheritance those stories built.** As in the town of Sleepy Hollow, too many Americans today are losing touch with the past — reframing or abandoning the founding stories and myths that built America. But those stories are too important to surrender, especially because no inheritance passes itself on. Someone must preserve it. Someone must teach it. And someone must make sure the next generation understands why it matters. That’s why Hillsdale College continues to teach great American works like “The Legend of Sleepy Hollow _._ ” The story is featured in our new **American Folktales** , an online course taught by Hillsdale College Professor Kevin Slack, who teaches about American politics, history, and culture here on campus. Professor Slack brings greater context and insight to familiar stories—revealing what memorable characters like Ichabod Crane and the Headless Horseman can teach us about human nature, early America, and the stories that shaped it. **The full short study is available now,** but to help you get even more from the course, **we’ve created a special American Folktales Study Guide that is available as a FREE download here:** **[https://info.hillsdale.edu/american-folk-tales](https://email.update.insidescooppolitics.org/c/eJyU0TuO2zAQBuDTUJ0EPkRZKlQs4hhJ4Q0SFykJmjOiB-FDEakN9vaBgvUB0s78mA-Y_-fVXC0FSv7VRpypFAMZDBC85z3kgiVHrA9K3kguh1aIVkzGukpvaHrbwKylGJexwVmcJs0npcTYPOZBAao7OtR3NTjd60kDgFXuJJYecWhoPu4JISahuNB9xx2_33GUzgmtOI6s5_sKtmJHqRBgcTmvaw5UyZUub74J86PWtTD1wuSFyQulJXcPCqGADdgh7ExebMSNnE3tksOvttqAhalLQR8x1U8ZkKkzV7LXlvPFRfSQAfE3k8Neoyl539wRWbdcVnSVkv9YRQTaI1NnjJbCx9DZuFryianzEzYH_M81pe7w7ncCfMZzqpgqU-cv337cPl9fXs33U_v1dmufz2m2GdY_FAKV4cR67g-sczk29f_Lepvl3wAAAP__65Gmkg)** Inside this special resource, you’ll find background on the stories, key themes and characters, discussion questions, and insights you may not have considered. And if you’d like to do even more, **please support Hillsdale with your tax-deductible gift to help keep courses like this—and the College’s nationwide educational outreach on behalf of liberty—FREE for all who wish to learn.** **When you give to this effort, you’ll also receive access to the course.** For now, please download your free guide and discover for yourself why readers have turned to classic American folktales like the “Legend of Sleepy Hollow” for generations. The Republican Party of Florida is preparing to elect its next chairman. On January 9, 2027, the party will decide whether to retain Evan Power or elect challenger James Campo.
But this contest is about more than two candidates. It raises a larger question:
**What does the Florida GOP need to examine about itself?**
A party asks voters to trust it with public power. How well does it govern itself?
### Who Has A Voice?
The chairman is elected by the Republican Party of Florida's State Executive Committee--not by a direct vote of Florida's millions of registered Republicans. Under party rules, only committee members in good standing may vote. At the annual meeting in odd-numbered years, officer nominations are made from the floor, and contested elections use secret paper ballots.
The Florida Phoenix estimates that approximately 240-250 people will participate.
That structure is not inherently improper. But it raises a question of representation: Do grassroots Republicans and county organizations have a meaningful voice in state-level decisions?
The chairman's position carries real institutional influence. The chair presides over State Committee and Executive Board meetings and has general supervision over party affairs. The Executive Board can act on the State Committee's behalf between its meetings, while the State Committee retains final authority over party matters not otherwise delegated. Nationally, the chairman is also one of Florida's three members of the Republican National Committee, alongside the national committeeman and national committeewoman.
Power points to statewide victories, registration growth, and his reported 350,000 miles of travel to local party events. Campo says he has visited 60 counties and argues that local activists have been alienated and deserve a stronger voice. Yet Campo is not an outsider; he has served as the party's assistant treasurer since 2023.
This is not simply insiders versus outsiders. It is a question of how influence is distributed.
### Five Questions For The Party
**Representation:** Does the party listen to the people who build it, or primarily to those who lead it?
**Accountability:** Are its constitution, bylaws, and rules followed consistently? Power says discipline was necessary to enforce party rules. Campo alleges selective enforcement. Both claims require scrutiny of the rules, records, procedures, and appeals.
**Political Direction:** What did the 2026 election reveal? Republicans retained statewide offices and control of the Legislature, but Democrats netted 16 seats in the House. The Republican House majority fell to 70-50, ending its two-thirds supermajority. The Senate also lost its Republican supermajority: Republicans hold 25 seats, two short of the 27 required.
The voter rolls raise another question. Between the October 5 book-closing deadline for the November 3 election and October 31, Democratic active registrations increased by a net 57,340, compared with 33,705 for Republicans. These are changes in active registration--not counts of new registrations--and they do not explain voter motivation. Still, the difference deserves attention. A registration advantage does not tell the whole story of political engagement.
**Organizational Integrity:** Are candidate access, internal participation, conduct, and disciplinary procedures handled fairly and transparently? Rules matter. So does how they are applied.
**Future Leadership:** What must change, and how will the next chairman be held accountable for delivering it? Campo pledges not to seek or hold public office while chairman. Power defends his record of engagement and electoral success. Beyond competing claims, the party needs clear priorities and measurable standards.
### Why This Matters
Why should an ordinary Florida Republican care about an internal party election?
Parties help recruit, support, and elect the people who govern. Their decisions influence leadership and priorities affecting families, the economy, the environment, and government--from schools and taxes to jobs, housing, land, and water.
The state party does not make every policy decision. But it helps shape who makes them.
### The Kitchen Table Perspective
A party can win elections and still have questions to answer. It can enforce rules and still need to demonstrate fairness. It can claim to represent the grassroots and still need to prove that the grassroots have a voice.
The people who build a party should not become an afterthought to the people who lead it.
**The question is not only who will lead the Florida GOP. It is whether the party understands whom its leadership is meant to serve.**

Peter,
We made our voices heard loud and clear on Election Day. We elected a Democrat to the U.S. Senate from North Carolina for the first time in nearly 20 years. We took back the majority. We sent an undeniable message to President Trump and the GOP that enough is enough – and we’re ready to move forward.
I’m so grateful to have people like you by my side, whether you’ve been with me since my first campaign or you’re just joining the team. I wouldn’t be here without you.
Now, Peter, it’s time to get to work.
**I’m ready to fight for all North Carolinians – _for the American people_ – but I’m going to need your help. As I put together my strategy for the first 100 days, I want to hear directly from my grassroots supporters about the issues that matter most to you.**
[**_Will you please take my new priorities survey and help shape my first 100 days in the Senate? On November 18, 2026, the GEO Group announced that it had sold the Northwest ICE Processing Center in Tacoma, Washington, to the federal government for $453 million.
**Nearly half a billion dollars in taxpayer money,** paid to a private prison corporation for a facility the government was already paying it to operate.
GEO expects approximately $340 million in proceeds after taxes and transaction expenses. It plans to use that money, together with operating cash flow, to finance a $500 million accelerated **stock buyback**.
The company will continue operating the detention center under a new ten-year federal contract worth approximately $1.5 billion, extending through October 2036.
The federal government gets the building. GEO gets the sale proceeds, the continuing detention business, _and_ the ability to reward its shareholders.

Meanwhile, the people of Washington State have spent years fighting for the right to send health inspectors into that building. More than 3,500 complaints have been submitted to the state Department of Health concerning conditions inside, including allegations of contaminated food and water, inadequate medical care, and unsanitary living conditions, alongside accusations of sexual assault and multiple detainee deaths.
(Four human beings have died in ICE custody at the Tacoma facility since it opened in 2004. Two died in 2024 alone. Washington State has also reported six attempted suicides since 2024 - although the fact that my husband directly witnessed two suicide attempts in one week in his unit, 1/16th of the entire facility, last year, strongly suggests that number is an undercount. One of those who died, Charles Leo Daniel, spent nearly four years in solitary confinement despite documented mental illness.)
GEO has resisted those inspections, even after unfavorable federal court rulings. The company now has an additional argument available to it: the facility belongs to the United States government.
Federal ownership does not automatically nullify state inspection laws, but it may significantly complicate the state's efforts to enforce them.
And that possibility was publicly identified long before the sale, including in my reporting:
[](https://substack.com/redirect/3113ffac-fba5-4922-a3aa-d0653e7833d2?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
Members of Congress warned about it. Attorneys and advocates warned about it. GEO's own corporate executives discussed the benefits of selling detention facilities to the federal government while retaining their management contracts.
The acquisition proceeded anyway.

## The corporation sells the building and keeps the business
To understand the Tacoma transaction, it helps to understand the financial strategy GEO has been explaining to investors since the spring.
In May, CEO of GEO Group **George Zoley** discussed ongoing negotiations with Immigration and Customs Enforcement to sell privately owned detention facilities to the federal government.
At the time, ICE was considering purchasing approximately ten operational detention centers. By August, GEO's leadership said the number under consideration could be larger.
The company's interest was straightforward: it wanted to liquidate valuable real estate without surrendering the extremely profitable business of operating detention facilities.
On its August earnings call, GEO put the strategy plainly:
"We are pursuing a potential sale of the buildings but we want to retain the business."
Let's take a look at that.
Traditionally, a company owning and operating a detention center has two related sources of economic value: the physical property and the contractual arrangement under which the government pays it to run the facility.
GEO recognized that these could be separated.
If the federal government purchased the real estate, GEO could collect the sale proceeds, reduce debt, repurchase shares, and continue earning revenue from management contracts.
The government would assume the responsibilities and costs associated with property ownership - maintenance, upkeep, utilities, etc - while GEO would remain the paid operator.
The arrangement had already been demonstrated in California.
On October 2, GEO completed the sale of three facilities in Adelanto--Adelanto West, Adelanto East, and the Desert View Annex--to the Department of Homeland Security for a combined $950 million.
GEO retained its operating role at those facilities under an existing contract running through 2034, including an option period.
The company reported approximately $705 million in proceeds after taxes and expenses, part of which went toward reducing its debt.
Then came Tacoma.
The new ten-year management contract took effect on October 28. GEO announced it publicly on October 29, describing a $1.5 billion federal commitment to continue providing security, maintenance, food services, medical care, transportation, and other support services.
Less than three weeks later, the building itself changed hands for _**another**_ $453 million.
Across Adelanto and Tacoma, GEO has now announced over **$1.4 billion in gross real-estate sales to the federal government since October 2**.
That figure represents sales revenue, not $1.4 billion in profit. The company incurs taxes and transaction expenses, and the properties have accounting values that must be recognized in determining gains.
**But ...** the financial transformation is substantial. GEO has exchanged ownership of detention real estate for a large infusion of cash while preserving the lucrative contracts that generate its operating revenue.
On November 18, CEO George Zoley celebrated the transaction and the company's continuing partnership with ICE. He also emphasized GEO's commitment to increasing shareholder value.
The business of incarceration has produced a remarkable new form of liquidity.

## Congress warned about the sale before it happened
On October 13, Representatives Pramila Jayapal and Emily Randall led thirteen members of Congress from Washington and Oregon in sending a formal letter to Homeland Security Secretary Markwayne Mullin and Acting ICE Director David Venturella.
They asked whether the administration intended to purchase the Tacoma detention center, how the government would determine a fair price, and whether private prison companies would continue operating facilities after selling them to the government.
The signatories included Washington Representatives Rick Larsen, Suzan DelBene, Marie Gluesenkamp Perez, Kim Schrier, Adam Smith, and Marilyn Strickland, along with five members of Oregon's delegation.
The letter described the federal government's growing program of detention-facility acquisitions and warned that federal ownership could be used to circumvent state oversight of facilities like Tacoma.
**The lawmakers cited reporting that both GEO and DHS had linked the acquisition plans to a deliberate strategy of avoiding state interference with detention operations.**
In August, KUOW had reported that DHS considered local government intervention an obstacle to the financial operation of privately run detention centers. GEO's leadership had also discussed the potential advantages of federal ownership in avoiding state oversight.
The congressional letter confronted those implications directly, especially in light of Washington's ongoing inspection litigation.
It also raised questions about conflicts of interest.
Acting ICE Director David Venturella had previously worked for GEO Group, and other administration figures involved in immigration enforcement had professional ties to the private detention industry.
Congress wanted to know what recusal procedures applied to former GEO employees involved in government decisions that could generate substantial financial benefits for the company.
The lawmakers requested answers by October 27.
The questions were basic to responsible public procurement. **Which facilities was ICE negotiating to buy? When were the purchases expected? What valuation methods were being used? Would the sellers retain operating contracts? How were conflicts of interest being handled?**
These are precisely the questions that _**should**_ be answered before hundreds of millions of public dollars are committed.
I have not found a publicly released response from DHS resolving those questions. A private response may have been provided; the public record reviewed for this essay does not establish that.
On October 28, the new ten-year operating contract took effect.
On October 29, GEO announced it.
On November 18, the federal government purchased the property.
The congressional warning had been on record for more than a month.

## Senator Murray raised the alarm again
On November 9, Senator Patty Murray sent DHS Secretary Mullin another letter concerning the Tacoma contract.
Murray, the senior Senator from Washington State and Vice Chair of the Senate Appropriations Committee, questioned the financial and operational implications of committing the federal government to another ten years of detention services at a facility already facing extensive complaints and litigation.
She also identified troubling provisions reportedly contained in a temporary contract between ICE and GEO.
According to Murray, the agreement included **language purporting to override state and local protections** and a provision **requiring the federal government to cover certain legal expenses incurred by GEO.**
There is a great deal to investigate in that language.
The private company has been fighting Washington State over the conditions under which it can operate. The federal government has reportedly agreed to cover some of its legal expenses. Now the federal government has purchased the facility.
**Putting the federal government in a direct posture of legal battle with one of its own States.**
The actual contract provisions, their scope, and any payments made under them need to be examined before drawing conclusions about what financial protections GEO has received.
But the prospect of taxpayers paying a private prison company's legal expenses while the company fights state health and safety oversight is disturbing enough.
Murray also questioned the contractual language declaring that, where federal and state or local requirements conflict, federal rules would control.
Federal supremacy is a constitutional doctrine. Its application depends on federal law and the nature of the conflict. A procurement contract cannot simply declare applicable state law irrelevant.
Among Murray's questions was whether ICE was considering purchasing existing facilities under the contracting model and, if so, which facilities were being considered.
She requested answers by November 20.
**The, the Tacoma transaction closed two days before that deadline.**
The timing does not _by itself_ establish that the closing was deliberately arranged to avoid congressional scrutiny. It does mean that DHS was proceeding with an acquisition of enormous financial and legal significance while a senior senator was formally seeking information about that very possibility.
**What did DHS know when Murray 's letter arrived? Had the purchase price already been agreed upon? Was a definitive agreement being prepared or executed? Did the agency inform Congress that the transaction was approaching completion?**
Those questions now belong in the investigation.

## Congress has been trying to execute oversight.
The congressional warnings were not confined to property ownership.
In December 2025, Murray and seven Washington House members demanded answers from ICE about deteriorating detention conditions, inadequate food and medical services, and barriers to legal counsel.
Jayapal and Randall conducted an oversight visit at Tacoma on October 29, the day GEO announced its new operating contract.
The delegation's concerns were sustained, documented, and repeatedly communicated to the federal government.
The sale proceeded against that backdrop.
## GEO lost the right to keep inspectors out. Now, conveniently, ICE owns the building.
Washington State's fight to inspect the Tacoma detention center has been going on for years.
In 2023, the Legislature passed House Bill 1470, establishing health and safety requirements for private detention facilities and authorizing inspections by the Department of Health.
GEO challenged the law in court.
The legal battle has moved through federal courts, injunctions, appeals, and repeated disputes over the state's authority to enter the facility.
In April 2026, Governor Bob Ferguson and Attorney General Nick Brown sought another court order after GEO continued denying inspectors access.
According to the Attorney General's Office, **state health officials had been denied entry ten times** , despite receiving more than 3,500 complaints.
Among the reported conditions were contaminated drinking water, food containing foreign objects, black mold, and inadequate medical treatment.
These are allegations and complaints requiring investigation; the total does not represent 3,500 independently verified violations.
But that is precisely why **inspection authority matters.**
When people are confined by the government, they cannot choose a different water supply, another medical provider, or a better place to sleep. They cannot simply leave an unsafe building.
The institution controlling their lives assumes responsibilities they cannot fulfill for themselves.
On July 9, U.S. District Judge Benjamin Settle granted preliminary injunctions supporting Washington's efforts to inspect the facility, subject to limitations concerning certain federally controlled areas.
GEO continued its appeal, with a Ninth Circuit hearing scheduled for November 30.
Then, in the middle of that dispute, the federal government purchased the property.

## What happens now?
The legal consequences are unsettled.
Washington's Department of Health has maintained that the state's inspection laws should remain applicable even if the property is sold to ICE. Officials have pointed out that the Tacoma facility is not situated within a federal enclave (such as a military base) and that GEO would remain the operator - putting it squarely within reach of Washington State laws, which regulate facilities _operated_ by private contractors.
Federal authorities, meanwhile, have asserted broad federal supremacy protections in their detention acquisition and contracting documents.
The state has a substantial legal argument that GEO cannot evade its obligations simply by transferring title to the federal government.
The federal government may claim that state inspections "interfere" with federal detention operations.
A court may eventually have to resolve those competing positions in light of the new ownership arrangement.
What matters now is that the purchase adds another complication to a prolonged effort to inspect a facility where people have reported serious health and safety problems.
There is also an uncomfortable possibility that deserves direct investigation: **Was changing the legal position of the facility one of the government 's reasons for purchasing it?**
That question is supported by more than speculation. Both congressional investigators and independent journalists, including me, documented discussions of federal ownership as a means of reducing state interference before the Tacoma transaction.
Whether that rationale influenced this particular purchase, and to what extent, should be established through the government's acquisition records and internal communications.
