## Glenville students still don't know where they'll go to school
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/04210dfb-0d33-4cb1-ace4-fb67941c56bb?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
Cleveland Metropolitan School District plans to start demolition at Glenville High School in summer 2027. The replacement campus is expected to include career training and a YMCA. Students are supposed to spend about two school years at a temporary site. The district hasn't said where. Some of these kids already moved once when Collinwood High School closed.
Alumni want the Glenville name to stay. I think it should.
And is there really no way to do this in phases? Take down the auditorium first, build classrooms there, then move the kids into those classrooms while you finish the rest. Maybe that's impossible on this site. If so, explain it. It seems unfair to send kids somewhere else for two years, especially the ones you've already made move. It seems like you could do better.

## Two Ohio abortion bills are headed to DeWine
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/3d0dc242-ee13-4983-84d8-a2e3754efcf8?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
We talked about these yesterday. **HB 347** would impose a 24-hour waiting period before an abortion. **HB 324** would add oversight requirements for certain medications and prohibit prescribing mifepristone for abortion through telemedicine.
The Senate passed both bills after they'd already cleared the House. Supporters say they improve informed consent and patient safety. Opponents say they conflict with the reproductive rights amendment Ohio voters approved in 2023. Now it's up to Mike DeWine.
[Statehouse News Bureau | Senate Republicans send two abortion bills to DeWine](https://substack.com/redirect/dee4bd25-83df-43f3-a69d-98299234dfa3?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)

## Ohio lawmakers fast-track a concealed-carry bill
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/9f26e8ec-6fc7-42a6-82d0-46dd2277e385?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
The Ohio House passed **SB 278, 61 to 33** , after adding language from a separate firearms bill. The Senate agreed to the changes. The bill would lower the minimum concealed-carry age from 21 to 18, expand which weapons a license covers, and loosen rules for firearms in vehicles. It's headed to DeWine.
Speaker Matt Huffman defended moving this quickly. Democrats asked why the bill got priority. I'd start with the gun lobby. And I'd like to know why leadership can put two bills together and get them through both chambers when other bills with bipartisan support can't get a floor vote.
[Statehouse News Bureau via Ideastream | Ohio lawmakers combine gun bills before sending them to DeWine](https://substack.com/redirect/10b8308c-0f96-4695-961c-ab66c6853eca?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) * [Ohio House journal | Recorded vote](https://substack.com/redirect/eb9f9c7b-48f5-4e98-9617-fa284216243c?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)

## The Ohio Senate votes to ban DEI programs in public schools
The Senate passed **SB 113, 21 to 10**. It would require public school boards to eliminate DEI offices and training programs and create a process for complaints. Republican Sens. Bill Blessing and Tom Patton voted with Democrats against the bill. It still needs to pass the House.
Sponsor Andrew Brenner says he's taking political ideology out of schools. Democrats say the bill undermines inclusion and equal opportunity. You see what's happening here. The incoming legislators are at orientation, and the people still in office are trying to get as much done as they can before the end of the year.
[Ohio Capital Journal | Ohio Senate passes the K-12 DEI bill](https://substack.com/redirect/eb7e8d41-b183-437c-92ae-57966626e78c?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)

## Republicans want to give Frank LaRose more power to audit Democrats
Republican Sens. Andrew Brenner and George Lang introduced **SB 494**. It would let the state auditor conduct performance audits of the offices of the governor, secretary of state, attorney general, and treasurer. Frank LaRose takes over as auditor in January. He'll be the only Republican among those statewide executive officeholders.
A blue frickin' nuclear bomb went off in Ohio. So now Republicans want the one statewide executive office they kept to have more oversight over the offices Democrats won. Would we be having this conversation if the election had gone the other way?
[Statehouse News Bureau via WVXU | Republicans propose expanding the state auditor's authority](https://substack.com/redirect/30c08928-5d79-4aea-ae79-d0adc8aefd3f?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
* * *
## Ohio's child marriage ban is still sitting there
**SB 341** would prohibit marriage before age 18. Ohio currently allows 17-year-olds to marry under limited conditions. Democratic Sen. Bill DeMora says the bill has the votes if leadership lets it come to the floor. Senate President Rob McColley says he supports the bill personally, and it still might never come up this session.
I'm trying to be fair about this. Say you have two high school sweethearts who've been together since seventh grade. They've both graduated, one is 18, the other is 17, and they say they want to get married before college. I can hear a parent saying, "They've been together six years. What's the fuss?"
And I still come back to the obvious answer. Wait until you're 18. The parental-rights argument gets messy fast, especially once you're talking about a 17-year-old and someone substantially older. I'd love to hear what you think. And if the bill has the votes, why can't we actually have that discussion on the floor?
[Statehouse News Bureau via WOSU | Why Ohio's child marriage ban may stall](https://substack.com/redirect/c44546bf-6b7e-491e-85c4-4b0b88e1931d?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
* * *
## The Ohio Senate makes time for ivermectin
Ohio senators passed **SB 249** , which would allow ivermectin to be dispensed without a prescription. Ivermectin is approved to treat certain parasitic infections. It became a political fight during the pandemic when people promoted it as a COVID treatment without evidence that it worked.
Man, they're busy. They found a way to get this one to the floor. The marriage-age bill is still sitting there. I think that tells you something about their priorities.
[Statehouse News Bureau | Ohio Senate approves dispensing ivermectin without a prescription](https://substack.com/redirect/fab3269b-4cb0-4983-a348-918c73b51c50?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
* * *
## Trump, Xi, and Putin meet. What came out of it?
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/e3d15a56-91f3-4414-b62a-136d9c9a6544?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
Donald Trump, Xi Jinping, and Vladimir Putin met in Shenzhen. They discussed nuclear risks, trade, and international security. Their joint declaration touched on United Nations reform and energy supply. They didn't announce a major nuclear agreement, and the declaration didn't address the wars in Ukraine or Iran. Trump said those issues would be discussed separately.
Then why the hell are you guys meeting? Ukraine is kind of a big deal. Iran is kind of a thing, too. It seems like having all three of you in a room would be the perfect time to talk about it. What did anybody come away with?
[Associated Press | Trump, Xi, and Putin hold three-way talks without a breakthrough](https://substack.com/redirect/29239edc-16e9-4633-a82c-b8e7ebe011ac?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) * [Joint declaration](https://substack.com/redirect/1e71802b-1e34-4429-b6b3-aadb8945278e?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
* * *
## Gulf attacks spread, and oil shipments through Hormuz fall
Iran targeted Kuwait and Bahrain following U.S. strikes on Iranian facilities. Saudi Arabia also reported damage from a missile attack in Riyadh. Preliminary shipping data cited by the Associated Press put crude shipments through the Strait of Hormuz at about **8.5 million barrels a day** , roughly half what was moving at the start of November.
I saw regular at Costco for $2.99. My stupid gas-guzzling car takes premium, so I'm still paying around four bucks. If shipping stays this disrupted, I wouldn't be surprised if that goes higher again. Unfortunate.
[Associated Press | Missile damage in Riyadh and falling crude shipments through Hormuz](https://substack.com/redirect/512088ed-6f14-4e23-9dac-5161259c6616?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
* * *
## Republicans are struggling to move another $350 billion spending bill
Senate Republicans are discussing a defense-heavy reconciliation package worth about **$350 billion**. House Republicans want spending cuts or other offsets. There's limited time before Democrats take over Congress, and some Republicans don't want to reopen the fight over Medicaid cuts.
Makes sense. If you're worried you'll lose Medicaid or you're trying to figure out how to pay next year's marketplace premium, you're already pissed. Start talking about another $350 billion in Washington and see what happens to the phones in those offices. People have every right to ask what Congress is doing about the bill they can't pay.
[Axios | Republicans struggle to move another reconciliation package](https://substack.com/redirect/21dac6ee-bf8a-46d9-baa1-e5dca3f578cd?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) * [KFF | What's driving proposed 2027 marketplace premium increases](https://substack.com/redirect/564f47d8-dee6-47ac-b7e4-53e637603099?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
* * *
## The United States loses its measles elimination status
The Pan American Health Organization withdrew the U.S. measles elimination designation on November 17. As of November 12, the CDC had reported **5,412 confirmed U.S. cases** this year. More than 5,000. That's the highest annual total in decades.
[Associated Press | Measles is no longer considered eliminated in the U.S. and Mexico](https://substack.com/redirect/c3736a8d-f429-4367-bc64-9d3df9a920c9?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) * [CDC | Statement on the loss of U.S. elimination status](https://substack.com/redirect/99ea74b8-91ec-4db4-9359-bcdca9cf9cdc?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
* * *
## Chris Van Hollen is challenging Chuck Schumer
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/6685322f-e53e-4859-a38f-3e0f2015a74f?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
Maryland Sen. Chris Van Hollen says Democrats need new leadership after the midterms. He says more than 10 senators are with him, though far fewer have said so publicly. Bernie Sanders and Michigan Sen.-elect Abdul El-Sayed are among his public supporters. Schumer has more people publicly backing him so far.
I don't know if Van Hollen can pull this off, to be honest with you. We'll see how many of those people are willing to put their names on it.
[Axios | The senators who could join Van Hollen's challenge to Schumer](https://substack.com/redirect/afbf64df-8caf-47f3-917d-13d8095c22dc?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
* * *
## What I want to hear from you
Cleveland needs to fix its electric infrastructure. The county is collecting taxes and giving out grants. The state wants to spend more money, too. How should they account for all of that to us, the people? _The people._ I was trying to do a Bane voice there, if you remember Batman. Anyway.
It feels a little vague, a little complex, a little opaque. Vague and opaque are probably the same thing, but you get what I'm saying. The city, the county, and the state all ask us for money. What should they have to show you about where it went and what they did with it? How could they do it better?
That was an angry day. I hope you have an absolutely amazing one.
## **Stay Angry.**

**Thursday, November 19, 2026 - **
_**Iran:** International Energy Agency: Iran war causes largest-ever disruption to global oil and gas trade. Iran says five oil tankers struck naval mines and caught fire in Hormuz. USS George Washington aircraft carrier leaves Gulf after three months. President Donald Trump threatens to "wipe out" Iran over potential dirty bomb attack; U.S. homeland security chief denies threat. Iran, China, and Russia demand end to military threats before full resumption of International Atomic Energy Agency inspections. Iranian Foreign Ministry spokesperson refuses NYT interview over report linking dams to military infrastructure._
_**Palestine:** Israeli forces kill two Palestinians in Gaza, wound woman. Israel ends central Gaza ground operation, reopens Salah al-Din Road. Israeli forces demolish agricultural structures and uproot olive trees in the occupied West Bank. Eight injured, mosque torched as anti-Palestinian violence escalates inside Israel. Save the Children: Palestinian victims account for nearly one third of violations against children worldwide._
_**Yemen:** Ansarallah missile attack damages Saudi investment fund headquarters. Sixty-four children killed, 64 injured in Yemen as fighting displaces 330,000 people, UNICEF says._
_**Lebanon:** Israeli airstrikes and artillery shelling continue to hit southern Lebanon despite ceasefire. U.S. sanctions Lebanese charity, businessmen, and gold firms over alleged Hezbollah financing._
_**U.S.:** House Democrats elect caucus leaders. House Democrats introduce bill to give removal orders an expiration date. Maryland Gov. Wes Moore says Democrats should not tie a government funding bill to ending the Iran war. U.S. security officials tell Congress they see no evidence cyberattacks caused tech outages. FBI deputy director declines to name a right-wing domestic terrorist group when pressed by House Democrats. California Gov. Newsom unveils plan to regulate AI. Kirkland & Ellis discloses $11.8 million of free legal work for Trump administration._
_**International:** UN's top court rules Myanmar committed genocide against the Rohingya. Russian strikes kill at least five across Ukraine. Iraqi court sentences six French nationals to life in prison for joining ISIL. Somalia expels UAE ambassador. Ethiopia and Eritrea move troops to border region in anticipation of war. IAEA chief says North Korea has expanded its Yongbyon uranium enrichment facility. U.S. and Venezuela sign deal to restore military ties, War Secretary Pete_ _Hegseth says in Caracas. Reuters: Trump official suggested Guyana consider ceding territory to Venezuela. Trump, Russian President Vladimir Putin, and Chinese President Xi Jinping hold first-ever trilateral summit in Shenzhen._
**This is Drop Site Daily, our free news recap We send it Monday - Friday**
[Upgrade to paid](https://substack.com/redirect/2/eyJlIjoiaHR0cHM6Ly93d3cuZHJvcHNpdGVuZXdzLmNvbS9zdWJzY3JpYmU_.gKqwL6nI0pwONoprTApbfbe7-8DRjjDFdIs0Km2_jJ0?&utm_medium=email&utm_source=subscribe-widget-preamble&utm_content=225665926)
* * *
# Iran
* **IEA: Iran war causes largest-ever disruption to global oil and gas trade:** The U.S.-Israeli war with Iran [caused](https://substack.com/redirect/e4230290-af56-42a9-b375-6e2e02dec77f?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) the largest disruption to the global oil and gas trade on record, resulting in cumulative losses of 2.8 billion barrels of oil and 60 billion cubic meters of gas supplies from the Gulf, the International Energy Agency (IEA) said Thursday. The conflict severely restricted shipping through the Strait of Hormuz, which normally carries about 20% of global oil and liquefied natural gas supplies.
* "The energy world will never be the same again as it was before the Iran war," IEA Executive Director Fatih Birol said. The agency said that the disruption could accelerate a global shift away from fossil fuels, potentially reducing oil demand by 4.4 million barrels per day by 2035 compared with its current-policy projections.
* Crude shipments through Hormuz fell to approximately 8.5 million barrels per day in November, half their prewar levels, according to data from maritime intelligence firm Kpler, which cautioned that the figure could rise in coming days. Total Middle Eastern oil exports across all routes, including pipelines bypassing the strait, fell to 64% of prewar levels, down from 97% in October.
* **Iran says five oil tankers struck naval mines and caught fire in Hormuz:** Five oil tankers struck naval mines and caught fire in the Strait of Hormuz on Wednesday and Thursday after entering "prohibited" shipping routes, according to Iranian authorities. Iran's regular Navy [said](https://substack.com/redirect/c3976ad2-1cbf-4daf-aeda-1a2a4efaac25?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) three tankers caught fire Wednesday in the eastern part of the strait after ignoring warnings and switching off their navigation systems. On Thursday, the Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps Navy [said](https://substack.com/redirect/122a4a89-3aae-4a1e-922e-c704198a60be?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) two additional supertankers struck mines, caught fire and exploded near the strait's southern coast.
* **USS George Washington aircraft carrier leaves Gulf after three months:** The USS George Washington aircraft carrier reportedly left the Gulf region after a three-month deployment, USNI News reported, citing a U.S. Navy official. Bloomberg reported that the carrier is likely returning to its base in Japan. Its departure follows the arrival of the USS Theodore Roosevelt in the Middle East, where it joined the USS George H.W. Bush. The U.S. military has not officially confirmed the George Washington's departure.
* **Trump threatens to "wipe out" Iran over potential dirty bomb attack; U.S. homeland security chief denies threat: **President Donald Trump [claimed](https://substack.com/redirect/2e8eb17d-7ea7-403c-9461-48e8e59ebc63?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) Iran was exploring the development of chemical and biological weapons, saying Tehran was "looking at gases, looking at bio," without providing evidence. Asked about the possibility of an Iranian attack on Washington, Trump told Fox News he did not believe one was likely but warned, "If it does happen, we wipe them out," adding, "I give you my word." Homeland Security Secretary Markwayne Mullin said during a congressional hearing Wednesday that Iran does not pose an imminent threat of a radioactive "dirty bomb" plot.
* **Iran, China, and Russia demand end to military threats before full resumption of IAEA inspections:** An end to military attacks and threats, along with credible guarantees against further strikes, is necessary before the International Atomic Energy Agency (IAEA) can fully resume inspections of Iran's nuclear facilities, Iran, China, and Russia said Wednesday. In a joint [statement](https://substack.com/redirect/6500bf99-cdb3-459b-962f-74efbf1cefc1?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) delivered at the IAEA Board of Governors meeting in Vienna, the three countries said U.S. and Israeli attacks on Iranian nuclear facilities had made normal verification activities practically impossible.
* Iran's ambassador to the IAEA, Reza Najafi, warned that Tehran would assess future inspection requests individually based on security considerations and would not grant unrestricted access while military threats persist. "We will not accept being bombed on the one hand while being asked ... to provide detailed information about our materials and sites and grant unrestricted access to them," Najafi said.
* He also warned that Iran could suspend its safeguards obligations if circumstances required, while maintaining that Tehran had not yet done so. The three countries said Iran had authorized all planned IAEA inspections at the Bushehr Nuclear Power Plant in 2026.
* **Iranian FM spokesperson refuses NYT interview over report linking dams to military infrastructure:** Iranian Foreign Ministry spokesperson Esmaeil Baghaei [said](https://substack.com/redirect/01d281de-cee3-4a58-a6c5-0622d8eb344d?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) he rejected an interview request from The New York Times over its reporting on Iranian dams and their alleged links to military infrastructure, accusing the newspaper of promoting narratives that could help justify U.S. and Israeli attacks.
* The Times [defended](https://substack.com/redirect/74d4394c-6974-406e-af5d-3fec0769346d?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) its reporting, saying it had accurately cited research and analysis by seven international experts and warning that portraying independent journalism as a pretext for violence was dangerous.
* However, two experts cited in the article publicly challenged the newspaper's framing. Nima Shokri, an expert on water security at the Hamburg University of Technology, [said](https://substack.com/redirect/b47ff79a-21bd-4261-80c1-a85619144b88?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) the proximity of dams to military targets neither establishes why they were built nor justifies attacks on them. Kaveh Madani, the former deputy head of Iran's department of environment, published an [article](https://substack.com/redirect/5aea6e63-5f10-4626-bbff-d90e1df21501?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) in Forbes refuting the Times' conclusions and said in a [post](https://substack.com/redirect/244085a8-cfa6-40f3-95c6-914077088918?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg): "My comments had nothing to do with dams or missiles!"

# Palestine
* **Israeli forces kill two Palestinians in Gaza, wound woman:** At least one Palestinian was shot dead by Israeli forces on Thursday on Salah al-Din Street in southeastern Gaza City, according to Al Jazeera.**** A Palestinian man also [died](https://substack.com/redirect/0c047a0c-a971-444b-a811-6adcec34c693?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) Thursday from wounds sustained in an earlier Israeli strike on the Bureij refugee camp, while a woman was shot and wounded in Khan Younis, southern Gaza, WAFA reported.
* Israeli forces also carried out demolitions overnight in central Gaza, following Wednesday's launch of a new ground operation targeting three areas west of the "yellow line."
* **Israel ends central Gaza ground operation, reopens Salah al-Din Road:** Israeli forces ended their ground offensive in central Gaza and reopened Salah al-Din Road, Gaza's main north-south artery, to traffic on Thursday, according to COGAT, the Israeli military body overseeing civilian affairs in occupied Palestinian territory. The operation, launched Wednesday near the "yellow line" northeast of Nuseirat refugee camp, forced hundreds of Palestinian families to flee. COGAT said Israeli forces had targeted "terrorist infrastructure" and warned Palestinians against crossing the yellow line or approaching Israeli troops.
* Hamas condemned the operation and forced evacuations as "a dangerous development and a flagrant violation of the ceasefire agreement," charging Israel of systematically confining Palestinians to an increasingly narrow area of Gaza and urging mediators to intervene immediately.
* **Israeli forces demolish agricultural structures and uproot olive trees in the occupied West Bank:**
* **Bethlehem:** Israeli forces [arrested](https://substack.com/redirect/4ae9820b-8265-4055-b649-1d4757fbfea9?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) five Palestinians in Beit Fajjar on Thursday, pursued olive pickers in Wadi Saif, and detained workers inside a stone factory, according to WAFA.
* **Ramallah and Al-Bireh:** Forces [demolished](https://substack.com/redirect/5419e4bb-d8e2-40fd-9314-e660efd0a2c5?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) agricultural structures and uprooted olive trees in Deir Ibzi. Late Wednesday, soldiers shot and wounded a 42-year-old Palestinian man in the foot during a raid on central Al-Bireh.
* **Nablus:** Israeli settlers [attacked](https://substack.com/redirect/f9cf2099-45e1-409f-b839-14f240d89e9d?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) a house under construction in Qabalan, smashing its windows.
* **Eight injured, mosque torched as anti-Palestinian violence escalates inside Israel:** Eight Palestinians were [injured](https://substack.com/redirect/5089be1b-375a-42ba-a21e-1cc075da98c6?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) in Kafr Qasim, a Palestinian city inside Israel, on Wednesday when an Israeli driver struck pedestrians at three locations, leaving two seriously wounded and three moderately injured. The town's popular committee described the incident as a deliberate attack fueled by anti-Palestinian incitement, while Israeli police said the driver was under the influence of drugs.
* Early Thursday, Israeli settlers set fire to a mosque in the village of Al-Dahi, near Nazareth, and spray-painted racist slogans on its walls.
* Separately, Israeli authorities forced a Palestinian resident of Ar'ara to demolish his unfinished home.
* **Save the Children: Palestinian victims account for nearly one third of violations against children worldwide:** More than 30% of the total violations against children globally in 2025 were committed against children in the occupied Palestinian territories, [according](https://substack.com/redirect/f47602fc-3a83-44ba-9fa3-8e5c0afa8117?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) to Save the Children's annual global report.
* Incidents of the denial of humanitarian access to Palestinian children represent more than 70% of the total incidents worldwide, while the killing and maiming of children in the Palestinian territories amounted to almost 40% of the global total. "The scale of harm to children in the occupied Palestinian territory is devastating," the report said.
* The report also found that Africa is home to the highest number of children living in conflict zones, accounting for about 260 million, or 44% of the global total, with an unprecedented two in five African children impacted.

# Yemen
* **Ansarallah missile attack damages Saudi investment fund headquarters:** A tower housing the headquarters of Saudi Arabia's Public Investment Fund in Riyadh [sustained](https://substack.com/redirect/5b99cdef-6eb9-4528-b526-bc4588070c98?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) damage following a reported Ansarallah missile attack on the capital, AFP reported Thursday. Witnesses said the 80-story tower, the tallest building in Riyadh's financial district, suffered damage to its glass facade and offices across several floors. The damage was reported hours after the Saudi-led coalition announced it had responded to an Ansarallah missile targeting Riyadh and that debris had fallen.
* Separately, the coalition said its air defenses intercepted and destroyed four Ansarallah ballistic missiles launched toward southern Saudi Arabia.
* **Sixty-four children killed, 64 injured in Yemen as fighting displaces 330,000 people, UNICEF says:** At least 64 children have been killed and another 64 injured in Yemen since fighting escalated on September 3, UNICEF [said](https://substack.com/redirect/235d84e8-2f56-481a-a891-bf9f6d62a528?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) Wednesday. More than 330,000 people, including 174,000 children, have been displaced, while at least seven schools and 28 health facilities have been damaged. UNICEF also reported that approximately one in three children screened by its mobile health teams were acutely malnourished.
* In Taiz City, more than 800,000 people have reportedly been cut off from humanitarian assistance, with water production down nearly 50% and food and fuel prices more than doubling.

# Lebanon
* **Israeli airstrikes and artillery shelling continue to hit southern Lebanon despite ceasefire:**
* **Nabatieh:** Israeli warplanes [struck](https://substack.com/redirect/cc41efc5-50a5-4a04-be52-d54d1b070d9a?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) the Ain Al-Samahiyah area between Zawtar Al-Sharqiyah and Mifdoun on Thursday, according to Lebanon's National News Agency. Israeli drones also exploded in the Hay Al-Dayaa neighborhood of Nabatieh Al-Fawqa and at a house in Choukine.
* **Marjeyoun:** Israeli warplanes launched two airstrikes on Qantara, while Israeli forces [fired](https://substack.com/redirect/b2b768d3-2ee6-46be-b838-d1f603d3770b?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) eight grenades toward Khiam.
* **U.S. sanctions Lebanese charity, businessmen, and gold firms over alleged Hezbollah financing:** The U.S. Treasury Department [imposed](https://substack.com/redirect/7a5e67f3-dd17-497d-b2dc-c0995bfaad66?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) new sanctions Wednesday on the Lebanese Wa Ta'awanu Association, three individuals, and two gold companies over alleged financial ties to Hezbollah. The Treasury described the association as a Hezbollah-affiliated charity that uses humanitarian services to conceal the group's activities. Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent said the sanctions were part of efforts to cut off Hezbollah's financial networks and counter Iranian influence in Lebanon.

# U.S. News
* **House Democrats elect caucus leaders:** House Democrats [elected](https://substack.com/redirect/de49aacc-7f46-49d9-b91b-06d142775857?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) California Rep. **Ted Lieu** House Democratic Caucus Chair on Wednesday, making him the highest-ranking Asian American House member ever.
* Democrats [elected](https://substack.com/redirect/281f5a18-d3b5-4cc1-bced-f97e19f4153e?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) Massachusetts Rep. **Katherine Clark** majority leader, making her the first woman to serve as House floor boss when Democrats take control in January. Rep. **Pete Aguilar** of California was elected majority whip, and Rep. **Joe Neguse** of Colorado was elected assistant speaker. All three ran unopposed and won by acclamation.
* Rep. **Lauren Underwood** [beat](https://substack.com/redirect/8a767eba-6062-4b83-a885-3a085381a83d?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) Rep. **Sara Jacobs** 143-118 to become House Democratic Caucus vice chair in one of the caucus' rare contested votes. Underwood, 40, co-chairs the caucus's policy and communications arm and has held leadership roles with the Democratic Congressional Campaign Committee.
* **House Democrats introduce bill to give removal orders an expiration date:** Rep. **Lateefah Simon** of California [introduced](https://substack.com/redirect/f4c51588-f8bc-4728-ae56-c6b96fc5e4cb?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) the "Protect Our Neighbors Act" Thursday, under which final orders of removal would expire after 10 years for people continuously present in the U.S. with no criminal conviction. Currently, these orders have no expiration date. Under the bill, an immigration judge could renew an expired order only if it had "clear and convincing evidence," and only if the renewal serves the public interest. The bill, co-sponsored by California Reps. **John Garamendi** , **Zoe Lofgren,** and **Juan Vargas** , was inspired by **Harjit Kaur** , a 73-year-old Bay Area grandmother who was detained at an ICE check-in in September 2025 and deported to India under a 2005 removal order. It follows Trump telling "60 Minutes" he would "love to do something on immigration" with Democrats, who take control of Congress in January.
* **Maryland Gov. Wes Moore says Democrats should not tie a government funding bill to ending the Iran war:** Governor **Wes Moore** , a potential 2028 Democratic presidential candidate, [told](https://substack.com/redirect/92390ecb-4720-465b-b5ec-7908864a5ea3?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) Politico that the Trump administration should end the war but that Democrats' effort to add language ending it to a funding bill is misguided. "I don't know why the American people are being asked to choose between ending a completely rudderless war that we're all paying for and saying, 'Can we please keep the federal government open?'" he said at the National Governors Association's New Governors Leadership Forum in Utah. Democrats in both chambers are pressuring leadership to draw a hard line on Iran war funding in any stopgap bill, which must pass before the Dec. 11 deadline.
* **U.S. security officials tell Congress they see no evidence cyberattacks caused tech outages:** At a House Homeland Security Committee hearing Wednesday, DHS Secretary **Markwayne Mullin** , Director of National Intelligence **Jay Clayton** , and FBI Deputy Director **Christopher Raia** said the outages that hit airlines, banks, Microsoft services, and the NSA's internal network were not linked. Mullin [said](https://substack.com/redirect/20b3f480-9da6-40b9-9d26-834da09e930b?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) he was "98% confident" they were not malicious activity by foreign adversaries but admitted he had "absolutely not" seen this many outages in so short a time. Clayton called them "separate service outages associated with maintenance and technical changes," and Raia said there is "no indication whatsoever" of malicious cyber activity.
* **FBI deputy director declines to name a right-wing domestic terrorist group when pressed by House Democrats:** FBI Deputy Director **Christopher Raia** [told](https://substack.com/redirect/43315224-5229-49b5-bd42-db8035e87a90?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) the House Homeland Security Committee on Wednesday that "there isn't" a right-wing organization he would name as a domestic terrorism group, after earlier answering "Yes, sir" when ranking member Rep. **Bennie Thompson** asked if any right-wing groups meet that test. A 2024 National Institute of Justice study, which the Justice Department removed from its website last year, found right-wing extremists have killed more Americans in ideologically motivated attacks than far-left or Islamic extremists.
* **California Gov. Newsom unveils plan to regulate AI:** California Governor **Gavin Newsom** , a likely 2028 presidential candidate, [released](https://substack.com/redirect/9095983b-9d58-49c1-a588-79c0d484e6be?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) a report, "AI Safety in 2026 and Beyond," on Wednesday in Washington that would let California officials intervene if AI models risk going rogue, embed independent safety monitors in labs, and order immediate shutdowns if developers don't quickly in "emergency situations." It also calls for giving the state the authority to cap companies' use of automation to develop advanced AI, and requires independent auditors to run regular safety tests on the technology.
* **Kirkland & Ellis discloses $11.8 million of free legal work for Trump administration: **The white-shoe law firm Kirkland & Ellis [disclosed](https://substack.com/redirect/6ef3e3f3-ad98-453c-b970-c8298b493592?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) to Congress that it has performed about 6,491 hours of free work valued at $11.8 million for the Commerce Department, the Pentagon, the Postal Service, the International Development Finance Corporation and an investment entity created under the U.S.-Japan trade deal, the New York Times reported on Thursday.

# Other International News
* **UN 's top court rules Myanmar committed genocide against the Rohingya:** The International Court of Justice [ruled](https://substack.com/redirect/77ac1d3f-daeb-461d-861c-66c99ff8715e?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) 9-6 on Thursday that Myanmar "has committed genocide against the Rohingya group in northern Rakhine state, in violation of its obligations under the Genocide Convention." ICJ President Yuji Iwasawa said Myanmar's security forces killed thousands of Rohingya civilians, with evidence showing about 10,000 killed. The court also noted that the soldiers carried out widespread sexual violence and extreme violence against children and attacked people while they fled. The "only reasonable inference," the court argued, is that Myanmar intended to destroy a "substantial part" of the group. The court ordered Myanmar to provide reparations and restitution, including facilitating the safe and voluntary return of Rohingya, finding the missing, and protecting the nation's Rohingya population from persecution. A military crackdown on the mostly Muslim minority in the country has forced more than 730,000 Rohingya to flee to Bangladesh. Thursday's ruling is the first time a state has been found responsible for genocide at the ICJ.
* **Russian strikes kill at least five across Ukraine:** Russian airstrikes on Wednesday [killed](https://substack.com/redirect/e6df67db-aed2-46d6-9b4e-0c6cb6f91338?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) at least four people and wounded 13 others in Odesa, and a separate Russian drone strike in Zaporizhzhia region killed a woman in Kushuhum. Following the Zaporizhzhia strike, local authorities ordered 184 people, including 85 children, evacuated from the nearby village of Balabyne. The strikes came a day after a Ukrainian attack on Russia's Kerch Bridge killed two people and collapsed part of the structure. On Wednesday, Ukraine also hit the Ilsky and Afipsky refineries in Russia's Krasnodar region.
* **Iraqi court sentences six French nationals to life in prison for joining ISIL:** The Karkh Criminal Court in Baghdad [sentenced](https://substack.com/redirect/04b0a9dd-91a6-4113-a720-d54274b85ae4?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) six French citizens to life on Wednesday for belonging to ISIL (ISIS), with French embassy representatives attending, the Iraqi News Agency reported. Sixteen French nationals have been convicted so far by the court in a trial that began in September, and all but one received life sentences, with the other sentenced to 15 years last month. Iraq received more than 5,700 ISIL detainees from over 60 countries in February after the U.S. moved them from Syria.
* **Somalia expels UAE ambassador:** Somalia [ordered](https://substack.com/redirect/d301b60d-6e50-42b1-8632-664e4bfcf4da?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) the ambassador from the United Arab Emirates to leave the country within 72 hours on Thursday, Reuters reported. President Hassan Sheikh Mohamud accused the UAE on Tuesday of giving economic and political support to some regional Somali governments opposing the federal government. In January, Somalia said it was terminating all its agreements with the UAE. The UAE trained hundreds of Somali troops from 2014 to 2018 and, according to senior Somali sources, still covers salaries and logistics for about 3,400 Somali military police and special forces in and around the capital, and it has committed hundreds of millions of dollars to ports and military infrastructure along the country's coast.
* **Ethiopia and Eritrea move troops to border region in anticipation of war:** The Ethiopian and Eritrean armies have [massed](https://substack.com/redirect/09845d0a-f926-41e2-8084-2fc793b5d51f?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) forces along their shared border, ACLED, the International Crisis Group, and people tied to militias in Tigray told Reuters. The buildup follows fighting that began in September between Ethiopia's federal government and Tigrayan rebels, with Ethiopia saying Eritrean forces crossed into Tigray in early October to back the rebels, which Eritrea denies.
* **IAEA chief says North Korea has expanded its Yongbyon uranium enrichment facility:** IAEA Director General Rafael Grossi [told](https://substack.com/redirect/8ddf1817-2311-47c6-9775-3f459e5eb15b?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) the agency's board of governors Wednesday that a further extension to the original Yongbyon enrichment facility has been under construction since mid-September and was "externally complete by late October," calling the ongoing expansion "extremely worrying." Pyongyang has not allowed IAEA inspectors into the country for years, so the agency monitors through satellite imagery and open-source information. North Korea calls Yongbyon "the heart" of its nuclear program, and Foreign Minister Choe Son Hui said last week that nuclear weapons are "the strongest guarantee" of its sovereignty while rejecting a G7 demand for complete disarmament.
* **U.S. and Venezuela sign deal to restore military ties, Hegseth says in Caracas:** U.S**.** War Secretary Pete Hegseth [announced](https://substack.com/redirect/38bcb796-9e74-4a6f-ba22-5b924701ba54?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) Wednesday during a visit with Venezuela's interim leaders that the two countries signed an agreement to reestablish military ties, ranging from joint training to intelligence sharing. He offered few specifics beyond "training together, partnering together, sharing intelligence, more defense equipment and capabilities together." During his remarks, he described the country as a "compliant security partner." Acting President Delcy Rodriguez, whose court-allowed term expired in July but who continues as head of state, said she hopes cooperation reaches "its highest possible level" to address common threats.
* **Reuters: Trump official suggested Guyana consider ceding territory to Venezuela:** The State Department's policy planning chief [told](https://substack.com/redirect/aa3e56a0-a76d-428b-96eb-9cd4964f98f1?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) Guyanese Foreign Secretary Robert Persaud in a September Washington meeting that he could help broker territorial talks with Venezuela's acting President Delcy Rodriguez, and floated the idea of Venezuela taking partial control of the Essequibo, which makes up the western two-thirds of Guyana. Guyanese officials were stunned by the remarks by Jeremy Lewin, who left the department in October, and quickly sought clarification, and State Department officials assured them U.S. policy on the border had not changed. Lewin told Reuters he held only "preliminary" and "confidential" talks at the White House's direction after Rodriguez wrote Trump in May seeking U.S. mediation. Venezuela has claimed the oil-, gold- and bauxite-rich region for over 180 years, while the U.S. and nearly every other country recognize it as belonging to Guyana.
* **Trump, Xi, and Putin hold first-ever trilateral summit in Shenzhen:** U.S. President Donald Trump, Russian President Vladimir Putin, and Chinese President Xi Jinping [met](https://substack.com/redirect/829d7ac2-23d1-4ca4-83ef-3ec643c6c98a?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) for less than 90 minutes Thursday on the sidelines of the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation meeting, the first time the U.S., Russian, and Chinese leaders sat together without other counterparts. Their joint statement, published by Chinese media, hinted that the U.S. might begin lifting some energy sanctions on Russia imposed after its 2022 invasion of Ukraine, but it did not address Ukraine or Taiwan. The statement also noted agreement among the three that immunity for state officials is "of fundamental importance," that the International Criminal Court must not abuse its authority, and that they should pursue UN reform and increased refined petroleum production.

This is Drop Site Daily, our free news recap We send it Monday - Friday Iran IEA: Iran war causes largest-ever disruption to global oil and gas trade: The U.S.-Israeli war with Iran the largest disruption to the global oil and gas trade on record, resulting in cumulative losses of 2.8 billion barrels of oil and 60 billion cubic meters of gas supplies from the Gulf, the International Energy Agency (IEA) said Thursday. The conflict severely restricted shipping through the Strait of Hormuz, which normally carries about 20% of global oil and liquefied natural gas supplies. "The energy world will never be the same again as it was before the Iran war," IEA Executive Director Fatih Birol said. The agency said that the disruption could accelerate a global shift away from fossil fuels, potentially reducing oil demand by 4.4 million barrels per day by 2035 compared with its current-policy projections. Crude shipments through Hormuz fell to approximately 8.5 million barrels per day in November, half their prewar levels, according to data from maritime intelligence firm Kpler, which cautioned that the figure could rise in coming days. Total Middle Eastern oil exports across all routes, including pipelines bypassing the strait, fell to 64% of prewar levels, down from 97% in October. Iran says five oil tankers struck naval mines and caught fire in Hormuz: Five oil tankers struck naval mines and caught fire in the Strait of Hormuz on Wednesday and Thursday after entering "prohibited" shipping routes, according to Iranian authorities. Iran's regular Navy three tankers caught fire Wednesday in the eastern part of the strait after ignoring warnings and switching off their navigation systems. On Thursday, the Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps Navy two additional supertankers struck mines, caught fire and exploded near the strait's southern coast. USS George Washington aircraft carrier leaves Gulf after three months: The USS George Washington aircraft carrier reportedly left the Gulf region after a three-month deployment, USNI News reported, citing a U.S. Navy official. Bloomberg reported that the carrier is likely returning to its base in Japan. Its departure follows the arrival of the USS Theodore Roosevelt in the Middle East, where it joined the USS George H.W. Bush. The U.S. military has not officially confirmed the George Washington's departure. Trump threatens to "wipe out" Iran over potential dirty bomb attack; U.S. homeland security chief denies threat: President Donald Trump Iran was exploring the development of chemical and biological weapons, saying Tehran was "looking at gases, looking at bio," without providing evidence. Asked about the possibility of an Iranian attack on Washington, Trump told Fox News he did not believe one was likely but warned, "If it does happen, we wipe them out," adding, "I give you my word." Homeland Security Secretary Markwayne Mullin said during a congressional hearing Wednesday that Iran does not pose an imminent threat of a radioactive "dirty bomb" plot. Iran, China, and Russia demand end to military threats before full resumption of IAEA inspections: An end to military attacks and threats, along with credible guarantees against further strikes, is necessary before the International Atomic Energy Agency (IAEA) can fully resume inspections of Iran's nuclear facilities, Iran, China, and Russia said Wednesday. In a joint delivered at the IAEA Board of Governors meeting in Vienna, the three countries said U.S. and Israeli attacks on Iranian nuclear facilities had made normal verification activities practically impossible. Iran's ambassador to the IAEA, Reza Najafi, warned that Tehran would assess future inspection requests individually based on security considerations and would not grant unrestricted access while military threats persist. "We will not accept being bombed on the one hand while being asked ... to provide detailed information about our materials and sites and grant unrestricted access to them," Najafi said. He also warned that Iran could suspend its safeguards obligations if circumstances required, while maintaining that Tehran had not yet done so. The three countries said Iran had authorized all planned IAEA inspections at the Bushehr Nuclear Power Plant in 2026. Iranian FM spokesperson refuses NYT interview over report linking dams to military infrastructure: Iranian Foreign Ministry spokesperson Esmaeil Baghaei he rejected an interview request from The New York Times over its reporting on Iranian dams and their alleged links to military infrastructure, accusing the newspaper of promoting narratives that could help justify U.S. and Israeli attacks. The Times its reporting, saying it had accurately cited research and analysis by seven international experts and warning that portraying independent journalism as a pretext for violence was dangerous. However, two experts cited in the article publicly challenged the newspaper's framing. Nima Shokri, an expert on water security at the Hamburg University of Technology, the proximity of dams to military targets neither establishes why they were built nor justifies attacks on them. Kaveh Madani, the former deputy head of Iran's department of environment, published an in Forbes refuting the Times' conclusions and said in a : "My comments had nothing to do with dams or missiles!" Palestine Israeli forces kill two Palestinians in Gaza, wound woman: At least one Palestinian was shot dead by Israeli forces on Thursday on Salah al-Din Street in southeastern Gaza City, according to Al Jazeera.** A Palestinian man also Thursday from wounds sustained in an earlier Israeli strike on the Bureij refugee camp, while a woman was shot and wounded in Khan Younis, southern Gaza, WAFA reported. Israeli forces also carried out demolitions overnight in central Gaza, following Wednesday's launch of a new ground operation targeting three areas west of the "yellow line." Israel ends central Gaza ground operation, reopens Salah al-Din Road: Israeli forces ended their ground offensive in central Gaza and reopened Salah al-Din Road, Gaza's main north-south artery, to traffic on Thursday, according to COGAT, the Israeli military body overseeing civilian affairs in occupied Palestinian territory. The operation, launched Wednesday near the "yellow line" northeast of Nuseirat refugee camp, forced hundreds of Palestinian families to flee. COGAT said Israeli forces had targeted "terrorist infrastructure" and warned Palestinians against crossing the yellow line or approaching Israeli troops. Hamas condemned the operation and forced evacuations as "a dangerous development and a flagrant violation of the ceasefire agreement," charging Israel of systematically confining Palestinians to an increasingly narrow area of Gaza and urging mediators to intervene immediately. Israeli forces demolish agricultural structures and uproot olive trees in the occupied West Bank: Bethlehem: Israeli forces five Palestinians in Beit Fajjar on Thursday, pursued olive pickers in Wadi Saif, and detained workers inside a stone factory, according to WAFA. Ramallah and Al-Bireh: Forces agricultural structures and uprooted olive trees in Deir Ibzi. Late Wednesday, soldiers shot and wounded a 42-year-old Palestinian man in the foot during a raid on central Al-Bireh. Nablus: Israeli settlers a house under construction in Qabalan, smashing its windows. Eight injured, mosque torched as anti-Palestinian violence escalates inside Israel: Eight Palestinians were in Kafr Qasim, a Palestinian city inside Israel, on Wednesday when an Israeli driver struck pedestrians at three locations, leaving two seriously wounded and three moderately injured. The town's popular committee described the incident as a deliberate attack fueled by anti-Palestinian incitement, while Israeli police said the driver was under the influence of drugs. Early Thursday, Israeli settlers set fire to a mosque in the village of Al-Dahi, near Nazareth, and spray-painted racist slogans on its walls. Separately, Israeli authorities forced a Palestinian resident of Ar'ara to demolish his unfinished home. Save the Children: Palestinian victims account for nearly one third of violations against children worldwide: More than 30% of the total violations against children globally in 2025 were committed against children in the occupied Palestinian territories, to Save the Children's annual global report. Incidents of the denial of humanitarian access to Palestinian children represent more than 70% of the total incidents worldwide, while the killing and maiming of children in the Palestinian territories amounted to almost 40% of the global total. "The scale of harm to children in the occupied Palestinian territory is devastating," the report said. The report also found that Africa is home to the highest number of children living in conflict zones, accounting for about 260 million, or 44% of the global total, with an unprecedented two in five African children impacted. Yemen Ansarallah missile attack damages Saudi investment fund headquarters: A tower housing the headquarters of Saudi Arabia's Public Investment Fund in Riyadh damage following a reported Ansarallah missile attack on the capital, AFP reported Thursday. Witnesses said the 80-story tower, the tallest building in Riyadh's financial district, suffered damage to its glass facade and offices across several floors. The damage was reported hours after the Saudi-led coalition announced it had responded to an Ansarallah missile targeting Riyadh and that debris had fallen. Separately, the coalition said its air defenses intercepted and destroyed four Ansarallah ballistic missiles launched toward southern Saudi Arabia. Sixty-four children killed, 64 injured in Yemen as fighting displaces 330,000 people, UNICEF says: At least 64 children have been killed and another 64 injured in Yemen since fighting escalated on September 3, UNICEF Wednesday. More than 330,000 people, including 174,000 children, have been displaced, while at least seven schools and 28 health facilities have been damaged. UNICEF also reported that approximately one in three children screened by its mobile health teams were acutely malnourished. In Taiz City, more than 800,000 people have reportedly been cut off from humanitarian assistance, with water production down nearly 50% and food and fuel prices more than doubling. Lebanon Israeli airstrikes and artillery shelling continue to hit southern Lebanon despite ceasefire: Nabatieh: Israeli warplanes the Ain Al-Samahiyah area between Zawtar Al-Sharqiyah and Mifdoun on Thursday, according to Lebanon's National News Agency. Israeli drones also exploded in the Hay Al-Dayaa neighborhood of Nabatieh Al-Fawqa and at a house in Choukine. Marjeyoun: Israeli warplanes launched two airstrikes on Qantara, while Israeli forces eight grenades toward Khiam. U.S. sanctions Lebanese charity, businessmen, and gold firms over alleged Hezbollah financing: The U.S. Treasury Department new sanctions Wednesday on the Lebanese Wa Ta'awanu Association, three individuals, and two gold companies over alleged financial ties to Hezbollah. The Treasury described the association as a Hezbollah-affiliated charity that uses humanitarian services to conceal the group's activities. Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent said the sanctions were part of efforts to cut off Hezbollah's financial networks and counter Iranian influence in Lebanon. U.S. News House Democrats elect caucus leaders: House Democrats California Rep. Ted Lieu House Democratic Caucus Chair on Wednesday, making him the highest-ranking Asian American House member ever. Democrats Massachusetts Rep. Katherine Clark majority leader, making her the first woman to serve as House floor boss when Democrats take control in January. Rep. Pete Aguilar of California was elected majority whip, and Rep. Joe Neguse of Colorado was elected assistant speaker. All three ran unopposed and won by acclamation. Rep. Lauren Underwood Rep. Sara Jacobs 143-118 to become House Democratic Caucus vice chair in one of the caucus' rare contested votes. Underwood, 40, co-chairs the caucus's policy and communications arm and has held leadership roles with the Democratic Congressional Campaign Committee. House Democrats introduce bill to give removal orders an expiration date: Rep. Lateefah Simon of California the "Protect Our Neighbors Act" Thursday, under which final orders of removal would expire after 10 years for people continuously present in the U.S. with no criminal conviction. Currently, these orders have no expiration date. Under the bill, an immigration judge could renew an expired order only if it had "clear and convincing evidence," and only if the renewal serves the public interest. The bill, co-sponsored by California Reps. John Garamendi , Zoe Lofgren, and Juan Vargas , was inspired by Harjit Kaur , a 73-year-old Bay Area grandmother who was detained at an ICE check-in in September 2025 and deported to India under a 2005 removal order. It follows Trump telling "60 Minutes" he would "love to do something on immigration" with Democrats, who take control of Congress in January. Maryland Gov. Wes Moore says Democrats should not tie a government funding bill to ending the Iran war: Governor Wes Moore , a potential 2028 Democratic presidential candidate, Politico that the Trump administration should end the war but that Democrats' effort to add language ending it to a funding bill is misguided. "I don't know why the American people are being asked to choose between ending a completely rudderless war that we're all paying for and saying, 'Can we please keep the federal government open?'" he said at the National Governors Association's New Governors Leadership Forum in Utah. Democrats in both chambers are pressuring leadership to draw a hard line on Iran war funding in any stopgap bill, which must pass before the Dec. 11 deadline. U.S. security officials tell Congress they see no evidence cyberattacks caused tech outages: At a House Homeland Security Committee hearing Wednesday, DHS Secretary Markwayne Mullin , Director of National Intelligence Jay Clayton , and FBI Deputy Director Christopher Raia said the outages that hit airlines, banks, Microsoft services, and the NSA's internal network were not linked. Mullin he was "98% confident" they were not malicious activity by foreign adversaries but admitted he had "absolutely not" seen this many outages in so short a time. Clayton called them "separate service outages associated with maintenance and technical changes," and Raia said there is "no indication whatsoever" of malicious cyber activity. FBI deputy director declines to name a right-wing domestic terrorist group when pressed by House Democrats: FBI Deputy Director Christopher Raia the House Homeland Security Committee on Wednesday that "there isn't" a right-wing organization he would name as a domestic terrorism group, after earlier answering "Yes, sir" when ranking member Rep. Bennie Thompson asked if any right-wing groups meet that test. A 2024 National Institute of Justice study, which the Justice Department removed from its website last year, found right-wing extremists have killed more Americans in ideologically motivated attacks than far-left or Islamic extremists. California Gov. Newsom unveils plan to regulate AI: California Governor Gavin Newsom , a likely 2028 presidential candidate, a report, "AI Safety in 2026 and Beyond," on Wednesday in Washington that would let California officials intervene if AI models risk going rogue, embed independent safety monitors in labs, and order immediate shutdowns if developers don't quickly in "emergency situations." It also calls for giving the state the authority to cap companies' use of automation to develop advanced AI, and requires independent auditors to run regular safety tests on the technology. Kirkland & Ellis discloses $11.8 million of free legal work for Trump administration: The white-shoe law firm Kirkland & Ellis to Congress that it has performed about 6,491 hours of free work valued at $11.8 million for the Commerce Department, the Pentagon, the Postal Service, the International Development Finance Corporation and an investment entity created under the U.S.-Japan trade deal, the New York Times reported on Thursday. 📥 Have a tip on Capitol Hill? Email DC Correspondent Julian Andreone at Julian@dropsitenews.com. Other International News UN 's top court rules Myanmar committed genocide against the Rohingya: The International Court of Justice 9-6 on Thursday that Myanmar "has committed genocide against the Rohingya group in northern Rakhine state, in violation of its obligations under the Genocide Convention." ICJ President Yuji Iwasawa said Myanmar's security forces killed thousands of Rohingya civilians, with evidence showing about 10,000 killed. The court also noted that the soldiers carried out widespread sexual violence and extreme violence against children and attacked people while they fled. The "only reasonable inference," the court argued, is that Myanmar intended to destroy a "substantial part" of the group. The court ordered Myanmar to provide reparations and restitution, including facilitating the safe and voluntary return of Rohingya, finding the missing, and protecting the nation's Rohingya population from persecution. A military crackdown on the mostly Muslim minority in the country has forced more than 730,000 Rohingya to flee to Bangladesh. Thursday's ruling is the first time a state has been found responsible for genocide at the ICJ. Russian strikes kill at least five across Ukraine: Russian airstrikes on Wednesday at least four people and wounded 13 others in Odesa, and a separate Russian drone strike in Zaporizhzhia region killed a woman in Kushuhum. Following the Zaporizhzhia strike, local authorities ordered 184 people, including 85 children, evacuated from the nearby village of Balabyne. The strikes came a day after a Ukrainian attack on Russia's Kerch Bridge killed two people and collapsed part of the structure. On Wednesday, Ukraine also hit the Ilsky and Afipsky refineries in Russia's Krasnodar region. Iraqi court sentences six French nationals to life in prison for joining ISIL: The Karkh Criminal Court in Baghdad six French citizens to life on Wednesday for belonging to ISIL (ISIS), with French embassy representatives attending, the Iraqi News Agency reported. Sixteen French nationals have been convicted so far by the court in a trial that began in September, and all but one received life sentences, with the other sentenced to 15 years last month. Iraq received more than 5,700 ISIL detainees from over 60 countries in February after the U.S. moved them from Syria. President Hassan Sheikh Mohamud accused the UAE on Tuesday of giving economic and political support to some regional Somali governments opposing the federal government. In January, Somalia said it was terminating all its agreements with the UAE. The UAE trained hundreds of Somali troops from 2014 to 2018 and, according to senior Somali sources, still covers salaries and logistics for about 3,400 Somali military police and special forces in and around the capital, and it has committed hundreds of millions of dollars to ports and military infrastructure along the country's coast. Ethiopia and Eritrea move troops to border region in anticipation of war: The Ethiopian and Eritrean armies have forces along their shared border, ACLED, the International Crisis Group, and people tied to militias in Tigray told Reuters. The buildup follows fighting that began in September between Ethiopia's federal government and Tigrayan rebels, with Ethiopia saying Eritrean forces crossed into Tigray in early October to back the rebels, which Eritrea denies. IAEA chief says North Korea has expanded its Yongbyon uranium enrichment facility: IAEA Director General Rafael Grossi the agency's board of governors Wednesday that a further extension to the original Yongbyon enrichment facility has been under construction since mid-September and was "externally complete by late October," calling the ongoing expansion "extremely worrying." North Korea calls Yongbyon "the heart" of its nuclear program, and Foreign Minister Choe Son Hui said last week that nuclear weapons are "the strongest guarantee" of its sovereignty while rejecting a G7 demand for complete disarmament. U.S. and Venezuela sign deal to restore military ties, Hegseth says in Caracas: U.S. War Secretary Pete Hegseth Wednesday during a visit with Venezuela's interim leaders that the two countries signed an agreement to reestablish military ties, ranging from joint training to intelligence sharing. He offered few specifics beyond "training together, partnering together, sharing intelligence, more defense equipment and capabilities together." During his remarks, he described the country as a "compliant security partner." Acting President Delcy Rodriguez, whose court-allowed term expired in July but who continues as head of state, said she hopes cooperation reaches "its highest possible level" to address common threats. Reuters: Trump official suggested Guyana consider ceding territory to Venezuela: The State Department's policy planning chief Guyanese Foreign Secretary Robert Persaud in a September Washington meeting that he could help broker territorial talks with Venezuela's acting President Delcy Rodriguez, and floated the idea of Venezuela taking partial control of the Essequibo, which makes up the western two-thirds of Guyana. Guyanese officials were stunned by the remarks by Jeremy Lewin, who left the department in October, and quickly sought clarification, and State Department officials assured them U.S. policy on the border had not changed. Lewin told Reuters he held only "preliminary" and "confidential" talks at the White House's direction after Rodriguez wrote Trump in May seeking U.S. mediation. Venezuela has claimed the oil-, gold- and bauxite-rich region for over 180 years, while the U.S. and nearly every other country recognize it as belonging to Guyana. Since the first day he stepped foot in Washington, Russell has strived to shake up the corrupt status quo and deliver real change for the American people. He believes adamantly that so long as the American people stand united, we can keep the American Dream alive for every citizen of our great nation. Russell is a dedicated husband to his wife, Bronwen, and a loving father to his son, James. The family lives in Murrells Inlet with their chocolate lab, Jasper.

During his seven-year tenure in the SC House, Russell fought to safeguard Constitutional liberties, lower taxes, and put the best interests of South Carolina families above all else. He climbed the ranks to become Chief Majority Whip, and also chaired the House Opioid Prevention Study Committee. Under Russell’s leadership, 18 policy initiatives to combat the opioid crisis were signed into law. Since the first day he stepped foot in Washington, Russell has strived to shake up the corrupt status quo and deliver real change for the American people. He believes adamantly that so long as the American people stand united, we can keep the American Dream alive for every citizen of our great nation. Russell is a dedicated husband to his wife, Bronwen, and a loving father to his son, James. The family lives in Murrells Inlet with their chocolate lab, Jasper. | | | | == | == ---|---|--- | | | Russell Fry for Congress PO Box 14641 Surfside Beach, SC 29587 | * | PAID FOR FRY FOR CONGRESS | | | | =

**SOUTHWEST, SOUTHSIDE FACE SHORTAGES OF SENIOR CARE, STATE REPORT FINDS** Not only are older adults in this region more likely to need help with daily activities, but they're less likely to find or afford that help...Del. Sam Rasoul, D-Roanoke, said that the rural regions of Virginia don't have the population density needed to support senior services. Rasoul serves on the legislative commission. The shortage of care isn't due to older adults not needing or using these services, he said. It's because business owners struggle to make the economics work in less densely populated areas. During a phone interview Thursday, Rasoul said that constituents contact him regularly about the high cost of long-term care and the lack of services that would allow them to age at home. Helping older adults remain in their homes generally costs less than assisted living or nursing home care, he said. Assisted living, in turn, typically costs less than nursing home care.

Hey folks,
The Tate brothers just bought themselves more time, and I'm not letting this story disappear. Their extradition hearings have been delayed until January, their lawyer is dragging Charlie Kirk and Russell Brand into the conversation, and the whole thing raises some serious questions about whether political connections could interfere with accountability.
We get into the legal fight, the MAGA influencers who've gone quiet, and why this story matters for the women and girls seeking justice.
Here's what we cover:
* [**00:01:25**] The Tate brothers' extradition hearings are delayed until January 14 and 15, 2027. What that means for their legal fight and the effort to attract attention from Trump's administration.
* [**00:03:39**] Their lawyer invokes Charlie Kirk and Russell Brand in an apparent attempt to rally MAGA influencers. We unpack the strategy and the hypocrisy surrounding it.
* [**00:06:54**] Why the MAGA influencer ecosystem keeps embracing controversial celebrities, and how attention, political influence, and allegations of abuse become tangled together.
* [**00:09:47**] As a practicing Catholic, I explain why using faith to dismiss serious allegations makes me so angry, and why genuine accountability matters.
* [**00:13:38**] Andrew Tate publicly appeals to Marco Rubio as his extradition fight continues. We discuss the legal process, the possibility of political intervention, and why I'll keep following this case.

This episode is about more than the Tate brothers. It's about what happens when influential people try to turn allegations of abuse into a political spectacle, and what we owe the people seeking justice. It's also about the young men being sold a version of masculinity built on resentment instead of responsibility, opportunity, and respect. We need better answers to their real economic struggles, and we need independent voices willing to keep asking difficult questions.
If you value conversations that put accountability, truth, and people ahead of political connections, help me keep them going.

Peter, we can’t fully understand the outcome of the midterm elections without looking at how the fair maps movement blocked the gerrymandering crisis from taking hold in Georgia. _**First,**_ we mobilized voters across the state to speak out against attempts by Governor Brian Kemp and the GOP legislature to redraw maps that would strip Black Georgians of their voting power. This public pressure forced Republicans to pause their plans to enact a mid-decade redraw — with the idea that they’d try again before the next election. _**Then,**_ we helped elect a Democratic governor and flipped the state house, making a new gerrymander IMPOSSIBLE next year. _**Now,**_ Republicans in Georgia are fully aware of the public backlash against gerrymandering, and the political price they’ll pay for manipulating maps. It was enough to stop Governor Brian Kemp from trying to redraw the state’s congressional map during a lame duck session. **This outcome is why we do this work, even when the deck seems stacked against us, Peter. # How to Extend a Photo on Your iPhone with iOS 27
Have you ever photographed a subject closer than you meant to, and wished you got more of the surroundings in your shot? With iOS 27 and later, you can use Apple Intelligence to extend your photo. This feature doesn't work on every photo, but will most likely improve over time.
## Why You'll Love This Tip
* **Learn how to extend photos you've taken with your iPhone or iPad.**
* **Tap the Edit icon, then the Apple Intelligence tools icon, then tap Extend. Pinch inwards with two fingers, then tap Extend.**

## How to Use the Extend Tool to Zoom Out on a Photo
### System Requirements
_This tip was performed on an iPhone 17 running iOS 27. These steps do not work for users running iOS 26, or for iPhones and iPads that cannot use[Apple Intelligence features](https://click.iphonelife.com/ga/click/2-17209627-5-0-261693-8633409-6b338b6ca6-9h66fc1464). Find out how to update to the _ _[latest version of iOS](https://click.iphonelife.com/ga/click/2-17209627-5-0-261693-8633410-80ab7eebd5-9h66fc1464)_ _._ Apple Intelligence allows iPhone and iPad users to alter pictures after taking them. One of these new features is the Extend tool, which uses AI to fill in the area around the subject when you zoom out on a photo.
1. Open the **Photos** **app** on your iPhone or iPad.

|
---
2. Tap the photo you want to edit, then tap the **Edit icon** at the bottom of your screen.

---
3. Tap the **Apple Intelligence Tools** icon.

---
### Enjoying Your Tip of the Day?
If you'd like to learn more about iPhone Life's premium paid subscription, [click here](https://click.iphonelife.com/ga/click/2-17209627-5-0-261693-3299547-1d40abe329-9h66fc1464)
4. Tap **Extend**.

---
5. Pinch two fingers inwards, or drag one of the black corners or lines along the perimeter of the photo to enlarge your picture.

---
6. Tap the **Extend button**.

---
7. If the feature can't be used on your photo, you'll see a notice that reads, **"None of the edges can be extended."**

---
8. If it is possible to use the Extend feature, it may take several minutes for Apple Intelligence to generate the new part of the photo.
9. You'll see a notification that reads, **"Your photo has been extended. Tap to see the original."**

---
10. You'll see your original photo. Tap the **check mark** to go back to the extended version, or the **X** to exit.

---

Now you know how to use the Extend tool in the Photos app on your iPhone and iPad. Be sure to check out our free [Tip of the Day](https://click.iphonelife.com/ga/click/2-17209627-5-0-261693-8633411-a7b2b16c6a-9h66fc1464) for more photo editing tutorials.

name: Andrew Sypher, Turning Point USA
subject: If you care about America, read this first
body:
I’m going to be blunt with you.

| | |
---
| | Friend,
---
I'm going to be blunt with you.

We are closer to losing this country than most people are willing to admit.

Not someday. Not "if things keep going this way."

Right now.

And the scariest part?

It's not happening in Washington. It's happening in classrooms.

High schools. Colleges.

Places where the next generation is being shaped -- or more accurately... reshaped.

If you've ever looked at what's coming out of our schools and thought: _" What happened to this country?" _

You're not wrong. You're seeing it clearly.

Because while most people are arguing online... while they're hoping things will turn around... while they're waiting for the next election to fix everything...

The other side is doing something far more dangerous.

They're raising the next generation.

Earlier. Faster. And with zero resistance in most places.

That's how countries are lost.

Slowly. Then all at once.

But here's the thing that should give a patriot like you hope...

There is one place where that trend is actually being challenged.

_And it shouldn 't even exist. _

**Just one year ago, Turning Point USA 's high school program -- which is now called "Club America" -- was in about 1,200 schools.**
That alone felt like a miracle.

Because starting even ONE chapter today takes courage most adults don't have.

Conservative students get mocked. Targeted. Threatened. Shut down.

And yet...

_They stepped up anyway. _

About that time, Charlie called me.

He didn't sound optimistic... He sounded urgent.

"Andrew, we've got to move faster."

I told him we were. He stopped me.

"No. You're not thinking what I'm thinking. I want to be in 35,000 high schools."

I actually laughed.

"Charlie... there aren't even 35,000 high schools in America."

"Okay," he said. "How many are there?"

"About 27,000."

And without hesitation: "Good. Let's do 27,000."

I remember sitting there thinking to myself... we're barely in 1,200 schools.

We didn't have the staff. We didn't have the infrastructure. We didn't even have the roadmap yet.

But Charlie wasn't fazed.

_" We'll figure it out." _

That was him.

He didn't wait for perfect conditions.

Because he knew something most people don't want to face: If we wait... _we lose everything. _

And now?

On Election Night, I was wearing two hats, Peter.

I was at a watch party for a candidate I’ve been working with as comms director this cycle, which meant running around to make sure every reporter in the room had the interview, quote, and camera angle they needed.

The second was my Her Bold Move hat. As our Director of Candidate Programs, I spend my days getting to know our candidates, figuring out what their campaigns need, and finding where Her Bold Move can help. Some days that means strategy, communications, media training, or making the right connection; other days, it means cheerleading and a whole lot of moral support.

I had a lot on my plate, but as the night went on and the good news kept rolling in, I was equally shocked and thrilled. Nights like this don’t roll around often in this line of work, and I am so thankful to everyone who made this possible.

[**Peter, will you take a moment to share with us your biggest takeaways from this November’s elections?**](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/143723248/661172903/616470623?nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9FQS9FQTAwNy8xLzg4NDk1IiwNCiAgIkRpc3RyaWJ1dGlvblVuaXF1ZUlkIjogImQ4MmExMjEzLTQzZTQtZjExMS05MWYzLTAwMGQzYTUzMzk3OCIsDQogICJFbWFpbEFkZHJlc3MiOiAiZHB3aWxsaXM2N0BnbWFpbC5jb20iDQp9&hmac=BiNg1KTH3LRZBjCb7vUU_boCxcg_Yx2lzFa7kJ_uuz4=&emci=9becea50-91e3-f111-91f3-000d3a533978&emdi=d82a1213-43e4-f111-91f3-000d3a533978&ceid=32015042)

These midterm elections showed me that change is possible everywhere, including in the places we’ve been told to give up on.

**By the time the dust settled, EVERY SINGLE Her Bold Move-endorsed candidate in South Carolina, Missouri, Arkansas, Alabama, and Indiana had won their races.**

**_That’s 19 women in five states where abortion is either banned or was back on the ballot this year, and all 19 of them are headed to their states’ halls of power._**

The best part? Research shows that communities and families fare better when women lead. That’s why Her Bold Move does this work, and it’s why I’ve made it my life’s work, too.

[**Click here to share your own takeaways from Election Night with us today.**](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/143723251/661172907/616470623?nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9FQS9FQTAwNy8xLzg4NDk1IiwNCiAgIkRpc3RyaWJ1dGlvblVuaXF1ZUlkIjogImQ4MmExMjEzLTQzZTQtZjExMS05MWYzLTAwMGQzYTUzMzk3OCIsDQogICJFbWFpbEFkZHJlc3MiOiAiZHB3aWxsaXM2N0BnbWFpbC5jb20iDQp9&hmac=BiNg1KTH3LRZBjCb7vUU_boCxcg_Yx2lzFa7kJ_uuz4=&emci=9becea50-91e3-f111-91f3-000d3a533978&emdi=d82a1213-43e4-f111-91f3-000d3a533978&ceid=32015042)

This was only the beginning. Now, let’s go work like hell to make sure all these women can pass the excellent legislation their constituents deserve.

In Hope and Gratitude,

Stephannie Lane
Director of Candidate Programs
